item.title: FCTA upgrades 20 PHCs, says pregnant women to get ambulance in 4 mins
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Capital Territory Administration FCTA has upgraded 20 primary health centres across the territory, declaring that it has cut emergency ambulance response to pregnant women to less than four minutes. Mandate Secretary, FCT Health Services and Environment Secretariat, Dr Adedolapo Fasawe, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja at the community engagement and inauguration of the renovated and upgraded Owner-Occupier Model Primary Health Centre PHC, Kubwa. She said the upgrade was carried out under the World Bank-supported Immunisation Plus and Malaria Progress by Accelerating Coverage and Transforming Services IMPACT project. To demonstrate how the emergency system works, Fasawe asked a pregnant woman to call one of the emergency lines. The ambulance reached the scene in less than four minutes. She said emergency response had been strengthened through the FCT Emergency Medical Services and Ambulance System (FEMSAS), which operates 24 hours a day, is free of charge, and brings local transport operators into the system to convey pregnant women during emergencies. According to her, the intervention goes beyond physical renovation. The administration has also built staff accommodation, provided modern medical equipment and installed solar-powered systems to guarantee 24-hour electricity and round-the-clock service. “The PHC is usually the first port of call for most residents. This is fundamental to improving health outcomes, reducing preventable deaths, and achieving universal health coverage. “This is just one of 20 primary healthcare centres across different communities in the FCT that were upgraded under the IMPACT project,” she added. On affordability, she said at least 1,000 vulnerable residents were being registered free of charge on the spot into the FCT Health Insurance Scheme under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund. The enrolment, she explained, entitles them to one year of free medical care in accredited public and private hospitals. Fasawe also commended the Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, for road construction and rehabilitation projects across the satellite towns, which she said had drastically reduced travel time to health facilities. She said the administration’s healthcare intervention rests on three pillars, which are access, affordability and quality, in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu. Fasawe urged traditional rulers and community leaders to take ownership of the upgraded facilities, monitor service delivery and make sure patients are not charged for free services. “Healthcare should not be a luxury reserved for a few. Quality healthcare is your fundamental human right,” she said. The Executive Secretary of the FCT Primary Health Care Board, Dr Dan Gadzama, said the Federal Government initiative began in 2021 with an initial completion date of December 2025. item.title: How to get a key cloner in GTA 6
item.description: The key cloner in Grand Theft Auto 6 allows you to steal keyless cars. As the most expensive cars in the game tend to be keyless, unlocking the key cloner is probably high on your priority list, but beware that it'll take a while to meet Randy, the key cloner expert.

item.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' gets final trailer, explaining why Steve Rogers is back and showing an epic battle with the X-Men
item.description: The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday just landed, and it finally puts the spotlight on our boy Steve Rogers. Avengers: Doomsday has been promising the scale and excitement the MCU has often been lacking since the Infinity Saga. Previous trailers played it safe, mostly setting up the conflict and introducing Victor Von Doom. Now it’s time for one last explosive look at the film before it tries to conquer cinemas next month. Disney and Marvel Studios have just released a “final trailer” that puts the focus back on Steve Rogers — no longer Captain America but still ready to use Mjolnir — and Thor as the veterans leading the New Avengers, former colleagues, the Fantastic Four, and even Fox’s X-Men (after some first-encounter fights, of course) against Doom and his followers. A few dodgy CG shots aside, it looks grand, and if you’re a big X-Men fan, it’s hard not to get goosebumps when Cyclops (James Marsden) finally gets to say the thing. The multiverse-spanning story is still largely kept a secret in this trailer, but at least we get a better sense of what the emotional stakes are for Rogers and how all these heroes can realistically work together against the greatest threat they’ve faced so far (even if most of them won’t get more than a few lines). (Image credit: Marvel) As for Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom, this isn’t his trailer, but the mysterious Latverian witches — who have fueled many theories online for months — are finally seen in motion. Doom has, however, received a simple but evocative poster that mirrors one of the original Iron Man ones. Even though Marvel Studios' honcho, Kevin Feige, has shot down the theory that this Victor Von Doom is a Tony Stark variant , you can’t stop marketing from doing the obvious things, it seems. We won’t complain. (Image credit: Marvel Studios) Avengers: Doomsday won’t fix all of the Multiverse Saga’s shortcomings, but at the very least, it looks like a proper fun time with more toys being mashed together than ever before and proper stakes. Right before Christmas, it’s hard to resist such a pitch. Avengers: Doomsday assembles on December 18, 2026, only in cinemas...Yes, it opens the same day as Dune: Part Three . item.title: Democrats fire starting gun on 2028 White House race
item.description: Democrats fired the starting gun Monday on the race to win back the White House, announcing plans for 12 debates to pick their standard bearer for 2028 as the party looks to build on its sweeping midterm election victory. The first debate is scheduled for June next year, setting the stage for what could be a crowded contest to select a challenger to the Republicans, who must find a successor to term-limited President Donald Trump. The announcement comes as Democrats celebrate their biggest majority in the House of Representatives since the early 1990s, with their victories this month transforming the balance of power in Washington and raising expectations for the next two years. “Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle,” Democratic National Committee chairman Ken Martin said. The party will hold five debates in 2027 and seven in 2028, the final one scheduled for March of that year. The debates will help voters choose the party’s presidential nominee through a series of state-by-state primary elections and caucuses, in which supporters select the candidate they want to face the Republican nominee in November 2028. Under new rules announced Monday, candidates seeking a place on the debate stage must pledge to denounce spending on their behalf by outside political groups, including those that do not disclose their donors. The requirement is intended to curb the influence of wealthy donors and so-called “dark money” in Democratic nomination contests, a longstanding demand of the party’s progressive wing. With a potentially large field, some debates could be spread across two nights, with a maximum of 20 candidates participating. No major Democrat has formally entered the race, but maneuvering is already underway among politicians seeking to become the party’s standard-bearer. Gavin Newsom, Josh Shapiro and Andy Beshear — the governors of California, Pennsylvania and Kentucky, respectively — are among those attracting attention as possible contenders. The post Democrats fire starting gun on 2028 White House race appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: British retailer Next downplays data breach at tech supplier
item.description: British retailer Next has become the latest high street name to find itself caught up in a cyberattack, although it insists the data accessed by hackers is "benign" and its customers have nothing to worry about. The clothing and homeware giant told investors on Monday that a third-party supplier had suffered a security breach, allowing an unauthorized party to access information relating to Next. The retailer says its own systems remain untouched and that, so far, there's no evidence that customer personal data has fallen into the wrong hands. "We have been informed that one of our third-party online suppliers has experienced a cyber incident which has resulted in unauthorized access to certain benign data relating to NEXT," the company said in its statement, which it shared with The Register . "We took immediate steps to investigate the nature and scope of the incident with the supplier." The breached supplier provides technology services to Next, and the "benign" information accessed is understood to be low-level data. Sensitive customer details, including addresses, passwords, and banking information, are believed to be unaffected. Next hasn't identified the supplier, explained exactly what the hackers managed to get their hands on, or revealed how much information was accessed, and declined to say when asked by The Register . However, the retailer has seemingly decided that the stolen data won’t be of much use to the criminals responsible. "Our investigations are ongoing; however, current evidence indicates that no customer personal data has been compromised," Next said. "The information affected is limited in nature and, based on our current assessment, cannot be used to facilitate fraud against our customers or NEXT." Next also stressed that its own IT infrastructure had escaped unscathed, saying it was "confident that NEXT’s own systems have not been compromised and that this remains an incident affecting the supplier's environment." Despite repeatedly describing the compromised information as harmless, Next says it is treating the incident "with the utmost seriousness" and is working with the affected supplier, law enforcement, and relevant regulators. The incident comes just weeks after fellow British fashion retailer Asos suffered a breach of its own , with hackers gaining access to customer information through third-party platforms. That attack, which came to light on October 6 when customers received an unauthorized push notification through the Asos app announcing that the company had been hacked, was traced to a social engineering scam. An attacker impersonated a trusted contact to trick an Asos employee into handing over login credentials, which were then used to access external platforms. Asos later admitted that the intruders had accessed customer names, contact details, and some account information, but passwords and payment card details were apparently off limits. item.title: Avengers: Doomsday Will Officially Bring Back One of the MCU's Best Heroes
item.description: The Avengers are set to get a little more help in December's Avengers: Doomsday . In an Instagram post on Sunday, Hailee Steinfeld confirmed she would return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Kate Bishop/Hawkeye while promoting her new movie Hexed . In the video, she pans to a director's chair with her name on it, like how the Doomsday cast was initially revealed in an hours-long stream last year.

item.title: Tennessee fined $250,000 after fans threw mustard and golf balls at coach
item.description: The Southeastern Conference has fined Tennessee $250,000 after fans threw a slew of objects toward LSU and their coach Lane Kiffin during a game the Volunteers won 27-13. SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey announced the penalty under the league's sportsmanship, game management and alcohol availability policies on Sunday. The trouble began with 3:14 remaining in the game when supporters in the Tennessee student section threw golf balls toward the Tigers bench. Play was halted for several minutes while the objects flew, and players gathered near the middle of the field to keep clear of any direct hits. Tennessee Volunteers fans react during the first half of the game against the LSU Tigers at Neyland Stadium on November 21, 2026 (Getty Images) “The golf balls have started being thrown at Neyland Stadium,” sports reporter Rhiannon Potkey wrote alongside video from the game. SportsCenter shared additional footage of a Tennessee staff member then carried a handful of golf balls and a mustard bottle to the sidelines. A message on the giant screen urged fans: “Keep your composure and practice good sportsmanship.” Kiffin ordered his players to exit through a side entrance once the game had finished rather than expose them to the home crowd a second time. “If cans or plastic bottles are used as projectiles or otherwise cause game management issues, the institution is subject to an immediate fine and suspension of the alcohol sales privilege," SEC rules state. The league has decided not to suspend alcohol sales at Tennessee for now, but it retains the right to do so in future. The hostility from Volunteers fans toward Kiffin stretches back to 2009, when he spent a single year as the university's head coach before leaving for USC. He came back for the first time in 2021, by then in charge of Ole Miss, and Kiffin and the Rebels were pelted with debris on that occasion too, some of it golf balls and a mustard bottle. Jeremiah Telander #22 of the Tennessee Volunteers celebrates after a 27-13 victory against the LSU (Getty Images) Tennessee students burned mattresses after Kiffin's departure, and in 2010 a Knoxville lawyer suggested renaming a wastewater treatment facility as the “Lane Kiffin Sewage Plant.” Tennessee coach Josh Heupel was asked about Kiffin's return, now as LSU head coach, during SEC media days this summer and referred back to the 2021 incident. “I certainly hope our fan base hasn’t cooled off.” Heupel said. “Whether it’s the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard or our sports stores, making sure that they got reinforcements on the golf balls ... hopefully Knoxville’s ready for his arrival.” The fine is Tennessee's second in quick succession, after the SEC fined the school $500,000 a month ago for allowing fans to storm the field following a 26-10 victory over then-No. 6 Alabama. item.title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan heartbroken over ‘crushing’ Colton McKivitz injury that’s similar to Fred Warner’s from last season
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan heartbroken over ‘crushing’ Colton McKivitz injury that’s similar to Fred Warner’s from last season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers ’ 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday came with a devastating cost. Right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a serious ankle injury in the second quarter, which left his teammates shaken as he was carted off the field in Mexico City. Head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed after the game that McKivitz suffered a fractured and dislocated left ankle. The injury is expected to end his season and reminded the 49ers of what Fred Warner went through last year . “We think it’s broken and dislocated, similar probably to Fred’s last year, so that was really crushing,” Shanahan said. “Colton’s had an unbelievable year. We care about all our guys, but it was tough to see Colton go down like that.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 49ers RT Colton McKivitz suffered what is believed to be a season-ending fractured and dislocated left ankle. “We think it’s broken and dislocated, similar probably to Fred [Warner]’s last year,” said 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan. “That was really crushing.” pic.twitter.com/LQRzK3RQzK — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 23, 2026 McKivitz went down late in the second quarter after Christian McCaffrey’s run ended with a pileup involving multiple players. McKivitz’s left leg got trapped underneath the pile, and his ankle was visibly injured when the players separated. Medical personnel eventually placed him in an air cast before carting him off. The injury is particularly difficult for San Francisco because McKivitz had been a dependable presence on the offensive line. He had started every game this season and entered Sunday’s matchup with an impressive streak of 270 consecutive snaps without allowing a quarterback hit, according to Pro Football Focus. McKivitz’s injury also closely resembles Warner’s ankle injury from last season, when the linebacker suffered a fractured and dislocated ankle and missed the remainder of the campaign. The 49ers will now have to adjust without their starting right tackle as they continue their push this season. Vederian Lowe stepped in after McKivitz went down and could be tasked with filling the vacancy moving forward. item.title: Rejoice! Luca Williams-Barnett’s assist has officially been credited on appeal!
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 21: Luca Williams-Barnett of Tottenham Hotspur during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Ipswich Town at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on November 21, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) | Offside via Getty Images I did not realize this had happened until it was already over this morning, but apparently after Saturday’s Tottenham Hotspur win over Ipswich Town, Luca Williams-Barnett was NOT credited with a goal and an assist to Dominic Solanke — just the goal. Stat trackers Opta initially did not give the assist to Williams-Barnett as it was initially judged to have taken a very slight deflection off of Ipswich keeper Christian Walton. However, after review, Opta has officially reversed course and has issued Luca his assist, and even posted about how that made him the second youngest player to ever score and assist in a Premier League game. However, to hear him tell it, it was James Maddison who pressured Opta to begin with. After the match, Madders apparently emailed Opta to ask why Williams-Barnett didn’t get credited with the assist, and then followed up on social media to take “credit” for Opta switching gears. I’ve watched the highlights of LWB’s assist many times over the past couple of days and I have to say I had no idea it initially wasn’t granted, because it’s so obviously an assist that it never crossed my mind. So kudos to Opta for looking at the evidence and officially making Luca second to Michael Owen in a trivia category. That’s pretty heady company to be keeping, and hopefully he’ll continue to do great things while at Tottenham.

item.title: York repeats as state volleyball champion while Victor, Mercy fall short
item.description: GREIGSVILLE – York accomplished what most high school girls volleyball programs only dream of: Back-to-back state championships. The Golden Knights defeated Hamilton (Section III) in straight sets (25-15, 25-16, 25-19) Nov. 21 to win the 2026 NYSPHSAA Class D title at Harding Mazzotti Arena in Glens Falls. They received a champion’s welcome upon returning home to Livingston County. Bailey Orman was awarded most valuable player of the Class D state tournament for the second consecutive year. The junior also reached a personal milestone in Glens Falls – 1,000 career kills. A parade of fire trucks from Cuylerville, Leicester and York accompanied Orman and the Golden Knights’ return home. Dozens of fans cheered – many waving yellow towels – as they deboarded a school bus with championship plaque in hand. “We didn’t really get into a groove until the very end of the season,” York coach Kaitlin Kolb said. “We worked hard over the postseason to keep meshing together and play our roles to the best of our ability. It really came together in the finals.” Welcome home York earned its spot in the Class D final by finishing 2-1 in pool play. Despite its loss to Candor (IV), York advanced with wins over Hamilton and Duanesburg (II). JJ Kane recorded a whopping 25 digs in the championship match, adding five kills and four assists. Tessa Goodell distributed 23 assists while Bree Parsons logged 13 kills, five digs and three blocks. Orman totaled 12 kills, 10 digs and two blocks against Hamilton. CC Biondo had 11 digs, Jordan Ray added 10 digs, and Fiona Grant chipped in four kills and four digs for York. “We have a great support system,” said Parsons, a senior. “I think that’s one of the reasons we’ve gotten so far – they were always here to support us. Being able to celebrate with them is so great.” Biondo and Kane led York’s defense all weekend, finishing with 40 and 36 digs, respectively, in pool play. Goodell, meanwhile, orchestrated the offense at setter, dishing out 51 assists in pool play to go with her 21 digs. Parsons and Orman each totaled 20 kills in pool play. Orman, who also had 20 digs, recorded her 1,000 th career kill. “My parents and all the people I started my career with,” Orman said, “have really helped me grow and gotten me over some challenging times.” Parsons and Goodell joined Orman on the Class D all-tournament team. Biondo won the sportsmanship award. “It still feels so unreal even though it’s the second time we’ve experienced it,” said Biondo, a senior. “Each year is so unique because we all need to learn about each other on and off the court. It makes a big difference when you do make those connections." Leaving a legacy York defeated Candor in the 2025 Class D state final. With much of its talent returning, the Golden Knights scheduled accordingly this fall, clashing with Section V powers such as Mercy, Hilton and CG Finney. Adversity accompanied their campaign. item.title: Rennie gets backing despite All Black defeats
item.description: Dave Rennie took the All Blacks role following the departure of Scott Robertson [Getty Images] All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has received the unequivocal backing of his bosses at New Zealand Rugby to lead the team through to next year's World Cup. Rennie's side have suffered back-to-back defeats in the November leg of the Nations Championship and have lost five times in the calendar year for the first time since 1998. "We have complete confidence in him," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said. "His position is not in question. He will take the team to the World Cup. That is not going to change." Rennie was appointed in March and started his All Blacks tenure in style, dispatching France and Ireland in the July part of the Nations Championship before a memorable victory over world champions South Africa in the Springboks' spiritual home of Ellis Park. But New Zealand lost the next three Tests against the Boks to fall 3-1 in the 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' [RGR] series, and, although two convincing wins over Australia retained the Bledisloe Cup, the All Blacks have endured a difficult tour of Europe. A first loss to Wales in 73 years was followed by an English rout in Twickenham, while the All Blacks have also been hit by the tragic death of their long-serving head of security Logan Cadwallader. The emotional toll of Cadwaller's passing along with the arduous schedule this year are thought to be two mitigating factors behind the dip in form, and New Zealand's administrators will review the impact of the RGR series when planning its return in 2030. Lancaster added that the union will look to make a call in the middle of next year as to whether Rennie takes charge of the team beyond the 2027 World Cup. "We will conduct a full campaign and season review following this year, as we always do," he said. "That will inform how we approach next year, but it will also inform our discussions around what the contract situation looks like beyond next year. "Our intention is to make all those decisions and have clarity before we go into the World Cup. Nothing has changed from when we appointed [Rennie] earlier this year. "He is a world-class coach. We went through the most rigorous appointment process that I have been involved in, which included spending time observing him coaching in Japan with his team and in his environment." We let the country down - All Blacks coach Rennie

item.title: YouTube Star Secures Shock DP World Tour Invite
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images YouTube content creator Peter Finch has accepted a surprise sponsor invite to play the AfrAsia Bank Mauritius Open on the DP World Tour. The event begins on December 10 and features a field that includes two-time Masters champion Bubba Watson. Finch, who runs a channel with over 850,000 subscribers, will compete against multiple tour winners in this 72-hole stroke play event. Finch announced the opportunity to his Instagram followers on Nov. 20, confirming that he will make his DP World Tour debut at the AfrAsia Bank Mauritius Open. The opportunity was not entirely new: Finch had discussed receiving the sponsor exemption on his Rough Cut Golf Podcast in October. The Path to the Field Finch’s journey to the professional stage has been steady but difficult. Finch has some professional tournament experience, including a tied-50th finish at the 2025 Egyptian Open on the Asian Development Tour. He also reached Final Qualifying for The Open in 2025 and finished tied for sixth at the 2026 Fairmont St Andrews Classic on the Tartan Pro Tour. The Mauritius Open will represent a significant step up in competition. These results showed he could handle pressure, yet the DP World Tour invite remains a step up in class. The tournament field features plenty of proven talent. South African stars Branden Grace, Thriston Lawrence and Dean Burmester are multiple DP World Tour winners. Casey Jarvis, another rising South African star with multiple tour victories, will also compete. They will be joined by Bubba Watson and defending champion Jayden Schaper. Regarding the opportunity, Finch wrote on Instagram, “I cannot wait to get out to Mauritius and compete against some of the best players in the world!” He noted that he has followed the event for a long time and sees this as a major milestone. “I remember watching this tournament over the years and just thinking what an amazing spectacle and an amazing privilege it would be to play at these courses, and that’s what we’re going to be doing,” Finch added in his post. Content Creation Meets Competition This dual role as competitor and creator adds a unique layer to the tournament narrative. While other players focus solely on their scorecards, Finch will be documenting the experience for his large online audience. Finch’s documentation of the experience could bring new eyes to the DP World Tour and highlight the challenges facing the sport. Finch’s participation also highlights the growing overlap between golf’s traditional professional tours and its enormous online content community. His tournament videos could give viewers an unusual look at the pressures of competing in a DP World Tour event. With more than 851,000 YouTube subscribers, Finch could introduce the tournament to golf fans who might not otherwise follow the DP World Tour. item.title: Emotional Diego Simeone thanks staff, family, players, fans, after landmark victory
item.description: Diego Pablo Simeone, head coach of Atletico de Madrid, is seen during the LaLiga EA Sports football match between Getafe CF and Atletico de Madrid at Estadio Coliseum in Madrid, Spain, on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Following Atlético Madrid’s 3-0 win over Getafe in La Liga on Sunday night, coach Diego Simeone celebrated becoming the coach with the most wins in the competition’s history, hitting the number of 345 victories in the tournament. “There’s no trophy, obviously, but it is a significant milestone as a coach, and I think that behind all this work over these 345 games, there are a lot of people, right? And I think, in my case, my wife, Carla Pereyra, honestly, she’s a very important source of strength that’s helped me get to this point, then there are the players, the club, our fans, but the people who are with you all day long, the people who support you, who stand by you, who hold you up, my daughters, my sons, the time we’ve dedicated to getting to where I am today, it moves me; honestly, it makes me happy,” an emotional Simeone reflected. “I don’t usually get excited about many things, but honestly, reaching this point has taken an incredible amount of work. There are many players who gave their all for the work we’ve set out to do, a whole lot of people who worked alongside me: Óscar Ortega himself, Germán Burgos, Juan Vizcaíno, Nelson Vivas, and so many others who were always there to support me, to give me the confidence to express everything I feel,” he continued. “And honestly, I wanted to expand a bit beyond the idea that, after 345 games, we’re still being called a defensive team, right? I think it was much nicer to thank the people I mentioned, because without them, it’s clear that all this energy that’s conveyed, and that I try to pour out, would never have come to be.” Insane. pic.twitter.com/yQEZKU9b3w — Atlético de Madrid (@atletienglish) November 22, 2026 Diego Simeone on Atlético’s dominance “I think we played an important game, where we immediately understood how we wanted to approach it. And honestly, the first-half goals helped us settle into the game better. We had chances to kind of seal it in the first half. We didn’t have that decisiveness we all always dream of, where every play turns into a goal. But still, the team created chances. We went into the second half in control and dangerous, because that 2-0 lead put us in a position where, if they’d made it 2-1, that would have sparked everything that happens when a home team scores a goal. And the result wasn’t quite enough for us—luckily, it came in the end. And well, I think we closed out an important game.” Simeone on whether he’s worried about chances missed “No, I’d be more worried if we didn’t have them.” Simeone on Johnny Cardoso’s substitution and Álex Baena’s form “It’s a bit of a mixed bag. item.title: Stock Watch: Which players impressed during Week 11 vs. Cardinals?
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs hosted the Arizona Cardinals in an important Week 11 matchup at Arrowhead Stadium, hoping to extend their winning streak to three games. The offense maintained a balanced attack, led by running back Emmett Johnson and veteran Travis Kelce, who scored twice. Patrick Mahomes spread the ball around, with Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen making plays alongside Rashee Rice at wide receiver. Xavier Worthy showcased his speed with an impressive fourth-quarter touchdown. The defense was ready, knowing the Cardinals had many issues, especially at quarterback. George Karlaftis tallied two more sacks, including a strip-fumble, in the victory. Nohl Williams was dominant in coverage, disrupting plays and showing versatility in the pass rush. Harrison Butker was perfect on the day, with two field goals silencing more critics and helping secure the team's victory. Check out how some of Kansas City's stars fared in the Chiefs' victory over the Cardinals: Stock Up: Travis Kelce The star tight end was in vintage form on Sunday with 6 catches for 74 yards and 2 touchdowns. He had his first game with multiple receiving touchdowns since Week 11 of 2022. Stock Up: Patrick Mahomes Mahomes was impressive again in Week 11, showing little concern for the Cardinals' defense. He finished the day with 27 completions, 324 yards, and 3 touchdowns. Stock Up: George Karlaftis The Chiefs pass rusher continues his Pro Bowl-worthy campaign, securing 2.5 sacks and one forced fumble on Josh Johnson, breathing more life into the once-criticized defensive line. Stock Up: Nohl Williams Williams was notably active in coverage and part of the early pass rush pressure Steve Spagnuolo dialed up. The second-year cornerback has taken a significant step forward in his young career. Stock Up: Harrison Butker Butker made two field goals and all of his PATs in the victory, quieting the noise around his future as Kansas City's kicker. This article originally appeared on Chiefs Wire: Stock Watch: Which players impressed during Week 11 vs. Cardinals?

item.title: Leaked: 1st pictures of new Arsenal home kit for 2027/28
item.description: Leaked: 1st pictures of new Arsenal home kit for 2027/28 Arsenal’s home shirt for the 2027/28 season has leaked, with a few major changes compared to this year’s home kit. Photo via FootyHeadlines.com Footy Headlines have leaked the design of Arsenal’s home shirt for the 2027/28 season, revealing some changes from recent seasons. The main one is the use of a tonal vertical striped pattern. Arsenal have generally only used a very subtle pattern (if any) on the front of the home shirt for the last few campaigns, but this one is much more pronounced. Then there’s the change to the Emirates sponsor logo, which just reads “Emirates”, rather than including “Fly Better”. Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images The shirt has also gone back to using the cannon logo, rather than the white crest on the 2025/26 and 2026/27 shirts. It also uses a v-neck collar, and there is very minor navy detailing on the collar and sleeves. Footy Headlines have revealed that the shirt will be accompanied by white shorts with red and navy trim, and red side stripes. The kit will use white socks with a dark navy hope and red ‘AFC’ lettering, and they’ve included a computer-generated mock-up of the full kit: Photo via FootyHeadlines.com As usual, the expectation is that the new kit will be released at the end of the current campaign. Whether or not it is released during the current campaign seemingly depends on whether Arsenal still have trophies to play for, as the Gunners have tended to stick with the existing shirt until the final game if they can still win something in it. If not, they’ve tended to show off the new kit in the final home game of the season. Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images For Premier League

item.title: 'It is difficult' - Real Madrid star Thibaut Courtois admits goalkeepers face impossible Ballon d'Or battle
item.description: Real Madrid v RC Celta de Vigo - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Thibaut Courtois has admitted he is baffled by what a goalkeeper must achieve to win the Ballon d'Or after being overlooked for the top prize in recent years. The Real Madrid number one expressed his frustration while also confirming his ultimate ambition to hang up his gloves in the Spanish capital. Frustration over individual awards Courtois has spoken candidly about the difficulties goalkeepers face in winning the Ballon d'Or , a trophy that has only been awarded to a shot-stopper once in history. Reflecting on his own career and the lack of recognition for his position, the Belgian international expressed a sense of resignation regarding the voting process. He pointed to 2022 as a year where he felt he deserved a higher ranking, noting that while Karim Benzema was a worthy winner, keepers are often relegated to the Yashin Trophy rather than the main prize. "I think I expected to be higher in 2022. Karim deserved it, but I think I should have been higher. We can perform brilliantly, but in the final minute [Kylian] Mbappe might score and that is what people will remember," explained Courtois, as quoted by AS . The veteran keeper, who recently extended his contract with the Merengues, highlighted that even standout seasons often fall short of the top individual honours. "It is difficult, I understand that, but I do not know what kind of season a goalkeeper has to have to win a Ballon d'Or. Some goalkeepers deserve to finish higher in the Ballon d'Or standings," he added. Commitment to Real Madrid Beyond his individual frustrations, Courtois made his long-term intentions clear by stating his desire to end his career at the Santiago Bernabeu. Having signed a contract extension, he emphasised that his primary goal is to remain healthy and continue winning trophies with the Spanish giants. "I'm very happy and proud to have signed for another year. My goal is to finish my career here; I need to stay healthy. I'm grateful for the club's confidence. The Champions League is tough, and with this format, everything is more open. I've won two, and I hope to win more," he confirmed. Hits back at Vinicius critics The conversation shifted to the form of Vinicius Junior, who has recently faced scrutiny for his performances . Courtois has launched a passionate defence of Vinicius, insisting that only Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are immune to dips in form. The Brazilian superstar has found himself under the microscope in recent weeks following a string of inconsistent performances for Los Blancos. However, his Belgian teammate was quick to shield him from the mounting scrutiny, reminding critics that demanding perfection every time he steps onto the pitch is an impossible standard. "We all have each other's backs. There's no need to be any closer to him specifically. He's happy, he's self-critical, and he knows he has to work. You can't be a number 9 or a number 10 all the tim

item.title: Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 are 40 percent off ahead of Black Friday

item.title: Mike Breen is still chasing a better call
item.description: Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Please don’t call Mike Breen the dean of NBA broadcasters. “This title of voice of the NBA that usually goes with whoever’s the NBA Finals announcer, I’ve never been comfortable with that,” he says. “Because I’m not the voice. There are so many voices.” Plus, there’s room for improvement. All the broadcasters in Breen’s circle want to get better. Yes, even the guy who has called the Finals since the second George W. Bush administration. “Every year I feel like I can get better at something, whether it’s having a more concise call, a better way to put into perspective what it means, the big picture stuff,” Breen says. This is not debatable. An NBA game feels important when Breen calls it. He’s at the point in his career – he’s called the Finals on TV since 2006; he’s been the voice of the Knicks (on radio, then TV) since 1991 – where he’s at the top of his profession. And that’s right: The Knicks, his boyhood team, are defending world champs after 53 years , thanks to a title run down a volcano, through a black hole, and over a rainbow. It’s all happening! The ego is in check. After all, there are so many voices. Breen did not have to talk to another media meatball after calling a Sixers-Pacers game the night before and hopping on a plane. During a 40-minute phone conversation in late October, the Fordham alumnus and “Bang!” enthusiast discussed the early part of his season, whether he cried after Game 5, and why his enthusiasm for the job has not waned. This interview was condensed for clarity and length. Have you rounded into form yet? That’s a good question. It usually takes me anywhere from 10 to 15 games before I feel like I’m in a real rhythm. I know that sounds odd with all the years I’ve done it, but once the NBA season ends, I’m off for pretty much four months. And I think my voice needs to round into form. And just the overall rhythm of getting back into the game and working with your partners, whether it’s on MSG with Clyde (Frazier) or whether it’s on ESPN with “Legs” [Tim Legler] and Richard (Jefferson). I don’t know if there’s any[thing] tangible: OK, I’m doing it this way now. It’s just more of a feel. The voice has to go through a bunch of games and highs and lows and high-intensity moments. There’s been a lot of changes with ESPN’s NBA crew in recent years. What kind of comfort level are you at now with Tim and Richard? Oh, it’s been wonderful. Last year, we worked almost every game together. In past years, they would kind of split up crews just to make schedules work and have everybody get the amount of games they’re supposed to do. But they made it a point to make sure we worked every game together going into the playoffs. So, by playoff time, we had a nice chemistry . I couldn’t be more pleased with how we came along. I really thought in the playoffs our chemistry was wonderful. “Legs” was the new guy, and Richard welcomed him with such open arms. They knew each other and were friendly before th

item.title: Australia vs. England 2nd T20I prediction, lineups and Carrara pitch report — who will win?
item.description: Australia vs. England 2nd T20I prediction, lineups and Carrara pitch report — who will win? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Australia host England at Carrara Oval on Tuesday in the second of five T20Is, with a 1-0 lead and a lesson about how thin the margins are in this series. The opener at the MCG could have gone either way. Harry Brook's boundary blitz gave England a strong platform, but Australia dropped six catches and still kept the visitors under 200. Then the hosts' new faces took over the chase. Sam Harper made 32 off 15, Nikhil Chaudhary hit 66 off 38, and Jack Edwards finished the job with a composed 25 off 11, winning with three wickets in hand in the final over. England now have two problems to solve. Will Jacks has a broken right hand and is out of the series, and their bowlers must find a way to stop an Australian batting order that hit hard from the first over. Australia vs. England prediction: Who will win? England's issue in Melbourne was not their batting but their bowling at key moments. Harper took 21 off Jamie Overton's first over, and Overton was hit for 12 off his first five balls when he returned in the 18th over. That spell took the game away from them. Australia have a question of their own. Adam Zampa went for 43 in four overs as he returned from back spasms. He has 20 T20I wickets at 15.45 this year, so he is trusted, but in an inexperienced side he needs to lead the attack. Australia have won their last five completed T20Is, while England's last five read LWWWW. The conditions may decide this one. Carrara is expected to help the spinners, and England have Adil Rashid and Liam Dawson to make the most of that. If they bowl better at the death and avoid giving Australia's hitters a free start, they should level the series. Cricket News Prediction : England to win. Riley Meredith was expensive in the opener, and Billy Stanlake and the uncapped Henry Thornton are options. item.title: New Zealand Rugby gives strong backing to Dave Rennie after record All Blacks defeat to England
item.description: New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has given its unequivocal backing to All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie through to the World Cup after back-to-back defeats to Wales and England. The tourists were stunned in Cardiff as Wales beat the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years, before suffering a record loss to England at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium on Saturday. Rennie was only appointed as Scott Robertson’s successor in March and took charge ahead of the Nations Championship in July, but has now suffered five defeats this year – including three to South Africa during the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour. NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster is clear, though, that the head coach retains their strong backing as the All Blacks prepare to meet England again this weekend. “We have complete confidence in Rens,” Lancaster said. “His position is not in question. He will take the team to the World Cup. That is not going to change. “He is a world-class coach. We went through the most rigorous appointment process that I have been involved in, which included spending time observing him coaching in Japan with his team and in his environment. “He is a very strong head coach. He provides absolute clarity to his team about how they want to play and absolute accountability about what is expected, what is measured. There are no gaps in information or understanding about the environment. The team love him. They are all behind him. They are all happy in the environment. The All Blacks suffered a record defeat to England (Getty) “Rens has incredible attention to detail. If you talk to Rens about the game he wants to play, he backs it all up by facts, evidence and data. Nothing is left to chance. Nothing is done on gut feel or assumption. He is in our mind the right man to take this team to the World Cup.” Rennie made a strong start to his tenure, beating France, Italy and Ireland in July before conquering the Springboks at Ellis Park in the first of a four-Test series. Two thrashings of Australia retained the Bledisloe Cup in October and Scotland were beaten in their November opener, but the head coach admitted his side “let the country down” after the Wales defeat. The squad have had to deal with the sudden passing of security chief Logan Cadwallader in Edinburgh, which is understood to have hit them hard, while the demands of a gruelling year of international action have also perhaps been felt. It is thought that both the All Blacks and South Africa will consider the impacts of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series , which also included four non-capped tour games, ahead of the next edition on New Zealand soil in 2030. As regards Rennie’s future, Lancaster intends to make it clear after next year’s Rugby Championship – which will feature a full schedule against Australia, the Springboks and Argentina. “Our intention is to make all those decisions before we go into the World Cup. Nothing has changed after we appointed Rens earlier this year,” Lancaster said. “We communicat

item.title: How the Mets rotation shapes up with the addition of Tarik Skubal
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WI - OCTOBER 11: Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts after pitching in the first inning during Game One of the National League Championship Series between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on Sunday, October 11, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images In case you have not heard the news yet, Tarik Skubal is a New York Met. You are likely going to be hearing a lot more about this over the coming weeks, especially with a looking lockout that could stretch into the season, robbing us of some extra time with Skubal (don’t worry about that, because he is also here for nine years). The Mets’ biggest need heading into the offseason was their starting rotation, and they addressed that by landing the biggest free agent not just at the position but in the entire sport. In doing so, the club added a two-time Cy Young Award winner who will immediately slot into the No. 1 spot in their rotation and give them the true ace they’ve been sorely lacking, arguably since Jacob deGrom left for Texas following the 2022 season. Skubal, who turned 30 years old on November 20, is coming off something of a down year, by his standards. He posted a 2.72 ERA, a 2.51 FIP, and 186 strikeouts in 158 2/3 innings across 26 starts. He started the year with the Tigers before heading over to the Dodgers and the year with 4.3 bWAR. He also pitched in two postseason games for Los Angeles and allowed three earned runs in 11 innings while striking out 14. Again, I would like to heavily stress that those numbers are pedestrian by his standards, and mostly because of what he did the previous two years in Detroit. In 2024, he finished with the best ERA (2.39), FIP (2.49), and bWAR (6.7) in the AL while leading the league in wins (18) and strikeouts (228). Unsurprisingly, he was a unanimous Cy Young winner while placing seventh in AL MVP voting. He followed that up by leading the AL (again) in ERA (2.21), FIP (2.45), and bWAR (6.4) while finishing with the best WHIP (0.89) and BB/9 (1.5) in the league en route to a second consecutive Cy Young Award (albeit not unanimous this time) and a fifth-place finish in AL MVP voting. So Skubal is set as the ace of the rotation, but where do the Mets go beyond the left-hander? Well lucky for them, they had a few young guys step up in 2026, which sets their rotation up to be in significantly better shape than it was heading into 2026, and that’s even before the Skubal signing. Lock: Nolan McLean Let’s get the easy one out of way. Nolan McLean, who finished fourth in NL Rookie of the Year voting, will serve as the de facto Robin to Skubal’s Batman. McLean was not quite as dominant as he was during his brief stint with the club in 2025, but he was really good. He posted a 3.16 ERA and 3.59 FIP in 179 2/3 innings across 31 starts, and he finished with 194 strikeouts and 3.0 bWAR. In total, he’s posted 4.6 bWAR since hi

item.title: The remains of a long-dead volcano on Mars | Space photo of the day for Nov. 23, 2026
item.description: null An image of Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, produced by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet. What is it? The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible new imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus. This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera. Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains. Despite its impressive height, it's still only about a medium-sized volcano for Mars, which is home much more impressively-sized volcanoes. For example, the planet's largest volcano Olympus Mons measures in at roughly 13.2 miles high (21.3 kilometers). Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, as seen by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Why is it incredible? While Tharsis Tholus might not be the tallest volcano on Mars, it is incredibly steep. It is steeper than Mauna Kea in Hawaii on Earth. To fully showcase the volcano's structure and topography in 3D, researchers actually exaggerated the vertical scale in this image, ESA reported . In addition to being steep and fairly tall, the volcano also has an interesting history. You can see that it is speckled with what look like small holes which are actually craters created by impacts from objects like asteroids. The volcano's current, unique shape is a combined effort by these impacts, environmental factors causing erosion and warping and ancient lava flows that left behind built-up material. The observations by Mars Express also reveals cracks and other imperfections in the volcano. All of these details might seem like superficial bits of detail, however every small crater, every lumpy cliffside and every worn down surface hides information about the planet's past. By studying features like volcanoes on Mars, researchers can piece together what the planet may have looked like in its ancient past. How active was this volcano? How did it interact with the landscape around it? Observations like this can hold the answers.

item.title: Why Santana Banner had one of Mizzou’s best defensive games in 2026
item.description: COLUMBIA, MO - NOVEMBER 21: Missouri Tigers safety Santana Banner (15) celebrates with teammates after intercepting the pass sealing his teams win during a SEC conference game between the Kentucky Wildcats and the Missouri Tigers held on Saturday November 21, 2026 at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium in Columbia MO. (Photo by Rick Ulreich/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of the key matchups between the Bluegrass State and Show-Me State this past Saturday night was Mizzou safety Santana Banner and preseason All-SEC tight end Willie Rodriguez. Banner, playing the STAR position, came in as Mizzou’s second-leading tackler, trailing Nicholas Rodriguez, while Willie Rodriguez has risen to be one of the better pass-catching tight ends in the SEC. Only Oklahoma’s Rocky Beers has more receiving yards among SEC tight ends. A sequence of plays on Saturday by Banner helped propel Mizzou to a 28-14 victory over No. 16 Kentucky, dropping the visitors’ playoff odds to 0.1%. Early in the third quarter, facing a second-and-goal, Banner matched up man-to-man in the slot with Rodriguez. Kenny Minchey didn’t hesitate on who he was going to in the end zone. His head turned right to his 6-foot-4 tight end. The ball was placed right into the numbers of Rodriguez, but the long arms of Banner prevented what could have been an 8-yard score. On the next play, third and goal, Minchey, under pressure from a cover-0 blitz, threw the ball behind Brock Coffman, but the sophomore wide receiver was blanketed by none other than Banner. Kentucky had to settle for a field goal, making it 21-6, instead of a one possession ballgame. Not allowing touchdowns in the red zone proved important for the Tigers. On the night, Kentucky reached Mizzou’s red zone seven times, but mustered just one touchdown in a two-possession loss. Banner himself, and we’ll get more into his statistics in a bit, was one of the catalysts in the Tigers’ defense responding after a poor performance against Georgia and Texas. “We played to our standard,” said Banner after Mizzou’s seventh win on the year. “Something we haven’t done the last couple of weeks.” Banner put the game on ice in another man-to-man coverage rep on Rodriguez in the fourth quarter with Mizzou up 28-14 with under three to play. Keeping his eyes on the quarterback while maintaining his inside leverage, Banner makes a fantastic play on the ball for his first interception of the season. THAT'S THE DAGGER !! @BeansBanner13 https://t.co/FwE0EkGnDt pic.twitter.com/BbaxLnFVsC — Mizzou Football (@MizzouFootball) November 22, 2026 “That’s their go-to guy. I think he’s leading the team in receptions, like 600 yards,” Banner said. “That was their top guy; they went to him to see if he could make a play towards the end of the game, and I just got there.” The Tigers didn’t completely shut down the Wildcats’ offense. item.title: Eric Kjar’s First Season at Weber State Continues into Playoffs
item.description: BOULDER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 12: Head Coach Eric Kjar of the Weber State Wildcats walks the field during the second quarter against the Colorado Buffaloes at Folsom Field on September 12, 2026 in Boulder, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Weber State had high hopes when it hired Eric Kjar to be its newest football coach following last season. In 2025 the Wildcats won just four games and made a coaching change in the middle of the season, relieving former head man Micky Mental of his duties in early November. Kjar came in over the offseason from the high school ranks, having coached at Corner Canyon High School. His successes were unparalleled in Draper as he went 112-10 with six state championships over the last nine seasons. That success, as Weber State hoped it might, has certainly spilled over in his first season at the helm in Ogden. Kjar’s team went 8-4 this fall and, as of Sunday, found out they’ll keep on playing. For the first time since 2022, Weber State is back in the FCS playoffs as an at-large selection out of the Big Sky and on top of that they get to host. Western Illinois comes to town this weekend and, with them, the chance to turn an already great first year for Kjar into a fantastic one with a win. Weber State made some real noise in the Big Sky this year. Whether it was the big Week 7 win over Idaho State or taking Montana State down to the wire the following week or taking down ranked UC Davis and Northern Arizona in back-to-back games over the last month, the Wildcats certainly did enough to earn their way into the postseason. It was a multitude of things that clicked well for them along the way but one of the biggest was the addition of game changers to the roster, starting with standout freshman quarterback Nate Dahle. Kjar and his staff brought Dahle in from Ridgeway High School in Millville, Utah and he’s been terrific. Dahle has thrown for over 2,500 yards and 25 touchdowns this season. He’s been the spark for an offense that was lacking one in recent years. Alongside Dahle has been the resurgance of Noah Kjar. The son of Kjar himself, Noah has actually been with the team for three years now but was sidelined for much of last season with an injury. Now with his father calling the shots, Kjar has come alive again for the WSU offense, hauling in 79 passes for 1,179 yards and 14 scores. His big play ability has been on full display this year and it’s certainly elevated the Weber State passing attack. ANOTHER NOAH KJAR TD @noahkjar_08 with a 27-yard TD catch for his 14th TD of the season! item.title: Alexander Zverev told he made a ‘costly’ mistake against Carlos Alcaraz at the ATP Finals
item.description: Alexander Zverev was denied a triumphant end to his best-ever season after he fell to Carlos Alcaraz in the championship match of the ATP Finals. Weeks after being crowned world number one for the first time in his career, Zverev lost to Alcaraz in straight sets, 6-2, 7-6. The German did not record a single win over either the Spaniard or Jannik Sinner in 2026 and has set the record for the fewest titles won in a season by an ATP year-end number one, with two. Photo by Marco BERTORELLO / AFP via Getty Images Greg Rusedski reacts to Alexander Zverev losing in Turin Reacting to Zverev’s defeat in an episode of ‘ Off Court with Greg ‘, former US Open finalist Greg Rusedski said: “He still has that little thing and them big moments arise, like it did at 6-3 in that second-set tie-break, where he doesn’t go big enough or aggressive enough at times, and that is very costly. “We saw that happen down under in the Australian Open, when he served for the match in that fifth set and got tight and lost that match, and then Carlos went on to win the Australian Open, hold all four majors, broke the record of Courier to make all the finals, and again became the fourth man in the history of our sport to hold all four majors as well as the end-of-season championships. “No Spaniard had done that before, Rafa Nadal is one of the players who hasn’t been able to do it. So from my point of view, Zverev got a little bit tight, didn’t play his best tennis in the finals, but what a year he has had. I kind of disagree with you a little bit, against Carlos I think he gets a little nervous, against Sinner in the Wimbledon final he was really good I thought. “So, you know give the credit, he deserves to be there because of what he has accomplished, won more Slams than anybody. But he’s got to prove it a little bit more against Carlos and Jannik Sinner, but he’s deserved to be world number one.” Photo by Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images Alexander Zverev urged to be more aggressive Rusedski continued: “Serving is so important against Carlos, especially indoors. We look at the matches, Shelton we said was the guy who could push him as well as Zverev had a chance to win. For me, I look at it…it’s the mental side. If you look at Sinner and you look at Alcaraz, when the big moments come what do they do? They hit the ball harder and play with more freedom. Zverev’s natural default is to wait for the guy to make a mistake. “The reason he has had such a great year is because he was willing to go after it, especially at Wimbledon this year, where he had never got to a Wimbledon final, never got past the fourth round or quarter-finals. That’s the difference, when he faces Carlos and Jannik, he has to go after it more in the bigger moments, and that’s something that’s not natural to him. But the problem he has as well is he has a little bit more scar tissue than Jannik and Carlos have. “Remember when he lost that final at the US Open, when he was supposed to win against Dominic

item.title: Former Seahawks corner Riq Woolen benched by Eagles for a familiar reason
item.description: ﻿Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images At Field Gulls, we keep tabs on former Seattle Seahawks players whether it’s going well or not, and there was one Week 11 game that went poorly for a couple of ex-‘Hawks. When the Pittsburgh Steelers lost to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, one of the headlines was former Seattle Seahawks receiver DK Metcalf getting tossed for two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties , the second of which was an attempted eye poke of Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean. Another notable ex-Seahawks in that game was Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen, whose own day didn’t go a whole lot better. Woolen didn’t play on defense for almost the entire second half, only to eventually come back later in the game when Quinyon Mitchell suffered a hamstring injury. Jonathan Jones replaced Woolen in the lineup while Riq’s snaps were limited to special teams. In his post-game media availability, Woolen confirmed he was benched and it’s for an all too familiar reason for Seahawks fans and maybe the Seahawks organization. Hear what Riq Woolen had to say about being benched for missed tackles before returning late in the game amid a rash of Eagles injuries at cornerback. pic.twitter.com/9gfW5ItI1C — NBC Sports Philadelphia (@NBCSPhilly) November 22, 2026 “I can’t say too much,” Woolen said. “It’s just the [coach’s] job. I mess up, they take me out. And I messed up, he took me out, and I just gotta be a great teammate just like how the next guy is. “It was just hard,” Woolen added. “I didn’t play the whole second half. To go in the last three, four minutes is tough. The DB position is a mental position more than physicality, so to be able to try to check back in mentally when you’ve been out so long is hard, but I have to be there for my guys no matter what. No matter how I’m feeling, it’s a team sport.” When asked if he was surprised if he was taken out, Woolen said he was not. “I had a talk with a coach before the game and then it was just basically saying I may be taken out a series just to help, you know, because I had a couple mental lapses. But it just turned into the whole second half and that’s how it went.” Putting two and two together, it looks as if this was the sequence that was the final straw for the Eagles coaching staff. This two-play sequence of missed tackles is presumably why the Eagles benched Riq Woolen, who confirmed that he was pulled from the lineup for almost the entire 2nd half before coming back in late for the injured Quinyon Mitchell. pic.twitter.com/JAc43a3yHl — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) November 23, 2026 “You know, we just wanted to reset there a little bit,” Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said of Woolen’s benching. He also noted that Woolen did “a nice job responding” after injuries forced him back into the game. item.title: Week 11 AFC West roundup, Chiefs keep pace with Broncos
item.description: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images While we already know that the Denver Broncos managed to get a win in Week 11, taking down the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 on Sunday, the Broncos are still in a tight battle for first place in the AFC West with the Kansas City Chiefs. Also, we have to take a peek at what the Los Angeles Chargers are doing to see if there’s any drama at the bottom of the division standings. Chiefs vs. Cardinals Score: 34-7 Chiefs Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 27/39 (69.2%), 324 yards, 3 TDs, 0 INTs RB Emmett Johnson: 23 carries, 105 rushing yards (4.6 ypc), 1 TD, 4 catches, 38 receiving yards TE Travis Kelce: 6 catches, 74 yards, 2 TDs EDGE George Karlaftis: 4 tackles, 2.5 sacks, 2 TFLs, 5 QB hits CB Nohl Williams: 3 tackles, 2 PDs, 1 QB hit This game was such a blowout that Mahomes barely even played in the fourth quarter, as Justin Fields got some reps off the bench. The Chiefs’ offense has been trucking along without Kenneth Walker III for the second week in a row, as the rookie, Johnson, has done a great job picking up the slack. Also, Kansas City’s defense has looked really sharp recently, allowing 13 or fewer points in each of the last three contests, while Karlaftis has really come alive as a pass rusher. The win allows the Chiefs to keep pace with the Broncos for first place. Denver has the advantage currently with a better record against common opponents, but this will be a battle of which team flinches first down the stretch. They split the season series, so one loss over the next seven weeks could be the difference. Next week: @ Bills (Thanksgiving night) Chargers vs. Jets Score: 27-24 Chargers lose Key Stats: QB Justin Herbert: 15/21 (71.4%), 131 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs, 8 rushes, 32 rushing yards, 1 rushing TD RB Omarion Hampton: 14 carries, 89 yards (6.4 ypc) WR Ladd McConkey: 5 catches, 37 yards, 2 TDs LB Troy Dye: 4 tackles, 1 sack CB Elijah Molden: 8 tackles After getting their first win last week, the Chargers had a chance to make it two in a row against the lowly Jets. However, Los Angeles continues to prove it is one of the worst teams in the league, getting outgained by 80 yards despite the three-point loss. The Bolts’ defense really let them down this time, allowing New York to go nine-for-11 on third downs while Geno Smith was hit just once and no defender had a pass breakup. item.title: Deontay Wilder gets new opponent for Fury vs. Joshua co-main event
item.description: Deontay Wilder beat Derek Chisora in his most recent match. | Richard Pelham/Getty Images Deontay Wilder will now box Martin Bakole in the co-main event of the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua card on Dec. 11 after the withdrawal of Zuffa Boxing cruiserweight Jai Opetaia, Netflix announced Monday. The card will take place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, and air live on Netflix. Bakole was originally slated to face Solomon Adebayo on the event but was elevated to the co-headliner after Opetaia was forced out due to a hand injury. Bakole, 21-2-1 as a pro boxer, fought to a draw with Efe Ajagba in his most recent appearance in May 2025, three months after losing to Joseph Parker for the WBO interim heavyweight belt. Wilder enters the ring with a 45-4-1 record and 43 knockouts, beating Derek Chisora by split decision and knocking out Tyrrell Anthony Herndon in his most recent matches. The main card, topped by a highly anticipated heavyweight showdown between Fury and Joshua, will also include Moses Jolly vs. Igor Macedo and Da’Mazion Vanhouter vs. Michael Essomba.

item.title: Saints vs. Bears: The good, the bad, and the ugly from Week 11
item.description: The Good: Defense All things considered the Saints defense played pretty well on Sunday. They held one of the better offenses in the NFL in the Bears to just 19 points and held Caleb Williams to 181 yards. The Saints defense also sacked Williams twice, and got four tackles for loss. They also got two takeaways, both through the efforts of Carl Granderson who tipped a pass that was intercepted by Danny Stutsman and forced a fumble that was recovered by Julian Blackmon. The Bad: Pass protection Tyler Shough was under duress all day as the Saints allowed 6 sacks. Shough had a hand in some of these as he left the pocket too early and scrambled into the defenders arms, but the Saints allowed Jeffrey Simmons to live in the backfield almost the whole game and allowed a total of 10 tackles for loss. The Ugly: More of the same Feels like I am writing the same thing every week, but the Saints continue to make no adjustments and simply nothing is changing. Once again they fell behind early, once again they turned the ball over multiple times, once again they squandered opportunities to get back in the game late, and once again they failed to adequately get the run game going. Travis Etienne Jr. actually became the first Saint to run for over 75 yards this year, but 46 of those yards came on one play. Take that away and he only averaged 2.3 yards per rush. They once again missed a field goal, and did not use Alvin Kamara in any meaningful way despite him scoring the only touchdown of the afternoon. The direction of the team is completely backwards and unfortunately, until changes are made, the results on the field will be the same.

item.title: What Aaron Rodgers did in Steelers defeat to Eagles hadn’t been seen in 20 years
item.description: Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers had a difficult afternoon as the Pittsburgh Steelers fell to a frustrating 19-16 defeat against the Philadelphia Eagles. The 42-year-old finished with respectable passing numbers on paper, but one remarkable statistic highlighted just how badly Pittsburgh’s offense struggled to get going. Rodgers averaged just 0.5 air yards per attempt in the first half, the lowest figure recorded in a half with at least 20 attempts since ESPN began tracking the statistic in 2006. Twelve of his 20 passes travelled no further than the line of scrimmage, underlining how little the Steelers threatened downfield. His struggles continued throughout the game as he completed 30 of 44 attempts for just 227 yards and one touchdown. Rodgers was also sacked five times, despite being under pressure on just 13 per cent of his dropbacks. That gave him a staggering pressure-to-sack rate of 71.4 per cent. Rodgers did at least show some mobility, rushing for 29 yards on five attempts. However, he received little help from DK Metcalf, who struggled before being ejected , while Max Hurleman offered some encouragement on his NFL debut. The Steelers managed just three points in the first half and could not complete their comeback attempt. They now sit at 6-4 and will feel they threw away a valuable opportunity against an Eagles team starting backup quarterback Joe Milton instead of Jalen Hurts. item.title: The secret injury clause that has Bayern Munich freaking out over Jamal Musiala
item.description: (Photo by S. Mellar/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Talk about a masterclass in negotiation. When Bayern Munich signed Jamal Musiala onto a bumper contract in 2025, there was speculation surrounding the details. Most drew attention to his salary increase, but a certain secret clause inserted by the player’s camp now has FC Bayern in a bind. According to a report by Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ), Jamal Musiala has a special guarantee in his contract that allows him to earn his full salary for six months in the event of an injury. With the emerging revelations about Musiala’s neurological issues, this clause has become a major sticking point for FC Bayern. Why does this matter? Most people don’t know this, but when a player gets injured playing in the Bundesliga, the club only has to pay six weeks of guaranteed salary before insurance takes over. So, if Musiala were to miss more than six weeks, Bayern Munich would have been off the hook. If it was a regular contract. Instead, with this clause, Musiala is guaranteed to be paid his substantial wages for up to half a year in the event of illness or injury. This means that, if Musiala experiences another episode and misses several months of football, he would still cost the club millions of euros despite not being able to contribute on the pitch. This is not the first time a clause like this has been granted by FC Bayern. Manuel Neuer also had something similar in his previous contracts, and Alphonso Davies is rumored to have one as well (though for a shorter duration of 3-4 months). For Musiala, the clause is doing what it’s supposed to. It is giving the player a semblance of security during this uncertain period in his life. For Bayern, however, it is turning into a massive liability. This may go some ways to explain the strange behavior by the executive team in recent days, though it is unlikely to win them any sympathy. With so many millions of euros on the line, and Musiala’s contract running to 2030, Bayern Munich are in desperate need of a solution to a problem they agreed to have. Join the conversation! item.title: MLB Hot Stove tracker: Live updates on latest news, rumors, signings and trades in 2026 free agency
item.description: MLB Hot Stove tracker: Live updates on latest news, rumors, signings and trades in 2026 free agency originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The heart of the MLB offseason is typically the first two weeks of December, but this isn't a typical offseason. A lockout is set to take effect at the end of the day on Dec. 1, ending all transactions until the owners and players agree to a new collective bargaining agreement. As we saw five years ago, that will likely take some time. 2021 offers an indication of how offseason transactions could play out: there was a flurry of activity leading up to start of the lockout, but plenty of significant moves had to wait until after the lockout was lifted more than three months later. If reports are any indication, though, No. 1 free agent Tarik Skubal has a strong chance to sign before the lockout begins, raising the level of intrigue around free agency. The Sporting News is tracking the latest MLB rumors, signings and trades before the lockout begins. Follow along below with the latest news. MORE: T racking the latest Tarik Skubal rumors MLB Hot Stove 2026: Latest news, rumors on signings and trades Mets add Paul Goldschmidt Date : Nov. 23 Source : Jon Heyman The veteran Goldshmidt isn't the star he used to be, but he can still defend at first base and hit lefties after serving as a platoon player with the Yankees. He will likely form a platoon with Jared Young at first base for the Mets next season. Tarik Skubal agrees to deal with Mets Date : Nov. 22 Source : J on Heyman The Mets have agreed to a nine-year, $450 million deal with Skubal, Jon Heyman and Jeff Passan report. Skubal's free agency ends more than a week before the lockout as the Mets make him by far the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history in terms of both total value and average annual value. item.title: Syracuse football: Orange lose more than bowl opportunity in Boston
item.description: CHESTNUT HILL, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 21: Justus Ross-Simmons #86 of the Syracuse Orange makes a catch against the Boston College Eagles during the first half at Alumni Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts. (Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images) | Getty Images If we’re being honest, there isn’t a ton of difference between 6-6 and 5-7….except where there is. After starting 2-4 and dealing with injuries to three quarterbacks, the Syracuse Orange had battled back and put themselves in position to end 2026 with a bowl bid. 6-6 would have shown fans that the team hadn’t quit and that maybe Fran Brown had earned some trust heading into 2027. Instead, Syracuse went to Boston College and watched as the familiar themes of this season: costly penalties, red-zone inefficiency and the nation’s worst kicking game resulted in a loss in a game the Orange had to have. Now it will take a Miracle on Irving Ave to get to 6-6 with a Notre Dame team that needs to make their final CFP case. 5-7 will be a point for those who want a new head coach. They will point to the California, Clemson and BC losses and say this team could have been 8-4….they will have a point there. The Orange gave away those three games and with them they would have had a solid bowl invitation. We can’t blame injuries for these games but Saturday’s game showed that Syracuse football needs to find ways to build depth. It also needs to stop giving away points with poor game management. At the end of the first half, simply running out a defensive sub when BC went into their fire-drill field goal scramble would have run out the half and saved three points. If you’re not down two scores, you take a short field goal (yes can’t assume it’ s a make) and maybe you get ahead of BC in the fourth instead of letting them continue to lead. If you’re worried about offensive plays in the red zone without your dynamic receiver duo of Hatcher and Russell, then call time out and tell the offensive coordinator to run something with them. If you notice your fifth-string running breathing heavy after a 29-yard run, get a substitute in and then run something different. Fans hate early timeouts but in games of this magnitude saving them for the final two minutes might not matter. (As an aside, there’s been this weird online conspiracy that Josh Gattis is calling the plays, but the funny part is all the people pushing this narrative weirdly still blame Jeff Nixon for red-zone play calling. Make that make sense) The next few weeks will be pivotal for Fran Brown. He’s got plenty of young players with game experience to build around, but he’s got to keep them, make the right call at quarterback, bolster the offensive line and figure out what he’s going to do with his coaching staff. None of those things will win back fans, but it’s the first step to keeping some optimisim going into the off-season. Fran Brown knows it’s important to win more games.
