item.title: Potential non-tendered free agent targets for Royals
item.description: Whew, the Kansas City Royals roster looks much different now than it did at this point even a week ago. The Maikel Garcia-to-Seattle trade was a swift move that opened the MLB offseason trade market, and adding Bryce Miller, Jose Ferrer, and Logan Evans to the 40-man roster should help address the team’s clear need for pitching ahead of the hopeful 2027 season – whenever that may be. The roster moves continued later in the week, when the team non-tendered reliever Anthony Gose, despite his 0.66 ERA in 14 appearances last season. Gose generated plenty of chase in his brief body of work and had above-average fastball velocity, but a 13.7% strikeout rate and a 4.84 SIERA were anemic even in the void that was the 2026 Royals bullpen. Without minor league options remaining, Kansas City would have had to carry him on the Opening Day roster to test whether there was more in the tank for the 36-year-old. Royals leadership has maintained that improving the pitching staff is the priority this offseason. Retaining Gose would have called into question how serious that effort really was, and the heat remains on Kansas City’s front office. The team also designated outfielder Kyle Isbel and reliever Nick Mears, later non-tendering them, making them free agents. They join a list of other non-tendered players around baseball, and they all fit a similar profile – rebound candidates, replaceable performers, or players who simply did not fit the team’s picture for next season. This is not a damning end for many of their careers, but rarely do these players go on to make teams regret the decision. The Royals non-tendered pitcher Taylor Clarke and outfielder MJ Melendez a year ago. Clarke’s 2026 performance in the Royals bullpen would have been a relief, but Melendez was hardly a factor for the New York Mets. Again, Clarke is the exception, and Melendez is the rule across the league. Of more than 70 non-tendered players last season, eight had noticeably solid seasons with new teams. Most of the remaining players missed 2026 to surgery, went to Asia, or barely pitched or played in the majors. David Fry, utility player 2026 stats: 214 PA (91 games), .201/.313/.364, 8 HR, 0 SB, 13.1% BB%, 27.6% K%, 93 wRC+, 0.2 fWAR 2027 projections (Steamer): 172 PA (41 games), .216/.299/.387, 6 HR, 1 SB, 9.4% BB%, 26.5% K%, 90 wRC+, 0.4 fWAR Royals fans might remember David Fry’s two-run homer in Cleveland’s 12-9 win over Kansas City in late September, but Guardians fans remember a lot more. Fry was a seventh-round pick by Milwaukee in 2018 out of Northwestern State and arrived in Cleveland as the player to be named later in a trade for J.C. Mejia. By 2024, he was an All-Star with a 129 wRC+ and 14 home runs while catching, playing first base, and covering left field. He also hit a walk-off homer in Game 3 of the ALCS. Not bad for a throw-in. The last two seasons have not been kind. Fry missed the start of 2025 recovering from an elbow injury, and his season ended in late September whe

item.title: Bears vs. Saints: Inside the Snap Counts, Stats, and What Was That Game Plan?
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 22: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears runs onto the field after his team's win against the New Orleans Saints at Soldier Field on November 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Did this feel like a Chicago Bears preseason game plan to anyone else? I’m not saying Ben Johnson looked past the New Orleans Saints, but the offensive game plan was run-heavy and fairly generic, and Dennis Allen’s defensive game plan was fairly vanilla. Perhaps, with the short week ahead to face the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving, they spent some of last week’s prep on their NFC North rival because they were confident they could beat the Saints. Chicago’s running game had a few explosives, but it was mostly a plodding, grind-it-out day, and Johnson stuck with it because I think he wanted to keep the clock moving. After they went up 16 to 0, it seemed like Johnson never felt the Saints had a chance to come back, and with the way his defense was playing, he was content to coast to the 21 to 13 win. Speaking of the defense, Allen was content to rush four most of the day and force the Saints to methodically work their way down the field. According to Next Gen Stats, the “Bears defense generated 24 pressures and 6 sacks against the Saints, their most pressures in a game since Week 9, 2018. Five of Chicago’s sacks came with a four-man rush, tied for the second-most by any defense this season.” Even though the score was closer than we all expected, the Bears controlled this game from start to finish. The Saints made it a one-score game before the half, but the Bears forced a three-and-out on New Orleans’ first possession of the third quarter, then went on an 11-play, 63-yard drive that ended in a field goal to push it to 19 to 10. Again, I don’t think they looked past the Saints, but back up two scores, this coaching staff felt confident they could ride it out because they were the better team, which is why they (possibly) went into it with that game plan in the first place. Tight end Colston Loveland alluded to a lack of enthusiasm. “I think we started slow and we didn’t really have the enthusiasm, I feel like, on a couple drives and then had turnovers and penalties, which hurts,” he said in his postgame presser via ESPN’s Courtney Cronin . “But I think there’s some good to take away for sure, too. I think it’s just in the run game, finishing, straining. I had a couple I fell off of that could have been two, three, four more yards. So I think that’s the difference.” There wasn’t any panic from the sideline during the game, and even in Ben Johnson’s postgame presser, he didn’t give off a disappointed vibe. The Good, Better, Best locker room speech, which was low-key after the narrow win over the Buccaneers, felt just as upbeat and as fun as usual. Again, I don’t think they looked past the Saints; I think they gave the Saints the attention they felt they deserved, with an eye toward Thursday’s ba

item.description: The presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has warned that any attempt to rig the 2027 general election could plunge Nigeria into a civil war. Hashim gave the warning during an interview on Symfoni Podcast, hosted by Olawale Oluwade, at the weekend, where he spoke on the state of the nation, insecurity and the credibility of the electoral process. He said Nigeria was already facing a dangerous combination of insecurity, political mistrust and weaknesses in the electoral system, which could create opportunities for armed non-state actors to exploit any post-election crisis. “The moment there’s a slight political crisis, the militia and terrorist groups, who are well organised, may take advantage of the political instability to expand and declare control in some states in the North and they will begin to press towards Abuja,” he said. The Accord Party candidate also criticised President Bola Tinubu’s handling of national crises, alleging that the President had repeatedly failed to remain in the country and confront challenges directly. “And President Tinubu will do the usual thing he does best, which is to run away. He is always away, he cannot stay to solve any problem; he will run away, he will take a flight out of the country,” Hashim said. He identified allegations that millions of fake names and artificial intelligence-generated photographs had been loaded into the Independent National Electoral Commission’s voters’ register as part of the concerns threatening the credibility of the 2027 elections. Hashim also questioned INEC’s level of preparedness less than two months before the election, while faulting the decision to postpone the clean-up of the voters’ register until after the polls. He warned that conducting the election amid rising insecurity and political violence, coupled with alleged electoral manipulation, could undermine the legitimacy of the government that would emerge from the exercise. “With the current insecurity, political violence and adding election rigging in 2027 will delegitimize the government completely and this could open space for non-state actors, insurgents, etc., already operating in 17 out of the 19 northern states to take advantage of the situation,” he warned. According to him, governors in most of the affected states have lost effective control of some rural communities, with insurgents allegedly imposing taxes on residents in areas under their influence. He said the development demonstrated the organisational capacity and financial resources available to the armed groups, warning that any political instability arising from the 2027 elections could further strengthen their operations. Hashim further cautioned that a disputed election could provide insurgents with an opportunity to expand their territorial influence and advance towards state capitals, potentially escalating the security crisis into a wider conflict. item.title: Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner Bitcoin Core developers have disclosed and patched a medium-severity bug that let an attacker temporarily freeze a node’s processing of blocks and transactions, a flaw first flagged by an AI scanner built by Block’s Spiral. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-117348, is fixed in Bitcoin Core versions 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1. The 30.5 and 31.3 releases shipped Friday alongside the public advisory, while 32.1 has carried the fix since Oct. 27. Affected versions run from 29.0 through 29.5, 30.0 through 30.4 and 31.0 through 31.2. The 29.x series has reached end of life and will not get a fix, so operators on that branch need to move to a newer release. How the Core bug worked Bitcoin Core keeps “orphan” transactions, whose parent transactions it has not yet seen, and asks peers that announce them for the missing pieces. Since version 29.0, the software builds a list of an orphan’s parents and checks each one against its mempool and filters before deciding what to request. A single inv message can carry up to 50,000 entries, and the software did not skip duplicates. An attacker could send a node an orphan with thousands of missing parents, then send messages repeating that transaction’s ID 50,000 times. “Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds, during which it processes no messages from other peers, including blocks,” the advisory said. Sending more messages could stretch the disruption out. The fix makes the node process each transaction announced in an inv message only once. The advisory describes a temporary denial-of-service problem and does not describe any way to steal bitcoin or permanently damage a node. It also does not say whether the bug was ever exploited. For a business running an affected node, the stalls could still matter. An exchange could be slow to credit deposits, and a miner could keep working on an outdated view of the chain while its node is stuck. An AI-found bug under a faster disclosure policy The advisory credits an automated LLM scan run through Elias Rohrer’s Project Loupe at Spiral, Block’s open-source bitcoin development arm. Bitcoin Core developer Gregory Sanders validated the finding and brought it to the project’s security team. Loupe is a free scanner that runs AI agents over open-source bitcoin code and only reports findings backed by a working test case. Bitcoin Core, BDK, LDK, rust-bitcoin, Cashu, Blockstream Jade, bitcoinj and SRI signed up for its first round of scans. Rohrer said on a recent podcast that Spiral started the project around March and began continuous scanning in May, with Bitcoin Core in the first batch. Loupe reported the issue on July 8. A developer known as Stutxo independently reported it on Aug. 4, the same day Sanders opened a pull request with the fix, which was merged two days later. The fix was backported to the 30.x and 31.x branches on Nov. 17. Bitcoin Core rated the bug “easily discovera

item.title: 2027: INEC warns against ‘rig and die’ slogan, debunks voting without PVC
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has cautioned politicians and their supporters against the use of the inflammatory slogan “rig and die” ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC), Mr Mohammed Haruna, gave the warning on Monday in Abuja, during the commission zonal forum with media stakeholders. Participants of the forum include the leadership of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Nigerian Institute of Social Media Analysts (NISMA), Newspaper Proprietors Association of Nigeria (NPAN), and media executives. Haruna represented by the Deputy Director, Information and Publicity, Wilfred Ifogah, warned that such rhetoric threatened the lives of electoral officials and voters. Speaking on the theme “Ethical and Professional Standards in Election Reporting ahead of 2027 General Election’, he noted that linking electoral offences to death was dangerous and could trigger mob violence at polling units. ”Consider the phrase “rig and die”, now widely repeated. Whatever its originators intend, though some people insist it is aimed only at those who rig, a slogan that links an electoral offence to death is dangerous. ”At the polling unit, the people most exposed are not powerful politicians but ordinary Nigerians serving as presiding officers, assistant presiding officers, collation officers and other ad hoc staff, alongside voters, party agents and observers. ”A charged crowd can easily mistake a delayed result, a technical difficulty or a rumour for rigging, and a mistake of that kind can never be undone. ”Rigging is a crime, and the Electoral Act 2026 prescribes penalties for it. The remedy lies in the law: vigilant observation, transparent results on IReV, formal complaints to the commission and the security agencies, and where necessary, the courts. ”The right to life is guaranteed by Section 33 of the Constitution, and no one may take it on suspicion,’’ he said. He urged political leaders to retire violent rhetoric and appealed to journalists not to amplify threats as headlines or trending hashtags. According to him, threats of violence are not robust political debate. They are offences and the security agencies have a duty to act on them. ”No journalists also should be intimidated for doing their work. A free press and a safe election go together.” The INEC national commissioner and chairman IVEC, also explained that the commission held itself to account, noting that any staff or ad hoc official who compromised an election would face the full weight of the law. ”The Act provides penalties for result manipulation, vote buying and the frustration of upload of polling unit results to the IReV. ”We are also working to have officials and materials at polling units by about 7; 30 a.m., on election day because delays breed suspicion,” he said. He also expressed confidence in Hamzat’s ability to build on the current administration’s achievements to expand economic opportunities and improve living standards in the state. ​In his address at the rally, Hamzat stated that his “PROMISE” agenda was designed to deliver broader democratic dividends if he is elected governor. item.title: Trade Fair leader seeks Lagos support for 5km road
item.description: By Elizabeth Osayande The newly re-elected President of the Balogun Business Association (BBA), Hon. Oscar Paul Ikechukwu Odogwu, has called on the Lagos State Government to partner with the association to rehabilitate the five-kilometre road network within the Trade Fair Complex. Odogwu made the appeal after securing re-election last Tuesday in an exercise whose results were announced by the Chairman of the Electoral Committee, Mr John Nwosu. Speaking on his priorities for the new tenure, he identified poor roads and inadequate parking facilities as major challenges facing the complex, which he described as an international centre for commerce. “The 5km road we have here is in a sorry state. We are trying to get government involved to make sure the roads and drainage are fixed, so that we have free flow of goods and services, trucks and cars moving around in the complex,” he said. He disclosed that his administration was also in discussions with Providus Bank on plans to establish a multi-level car park within the complex. “We don’t have much space inside our complex. What we plan to do is to have a multi-level car park, so our customers and our people will have somewhere to park. But if we can partner with government, that will be fine too,” he said. Odogwu also dismissed reports of tension and crisis surrounding the election, insisting that the exercise was peaceful and credible. “There is no crisis. Not even one person was touched. It is the work of rumour mongers trying to dissuade people from coming out to vote,” he said. He attributed the credibility of the election to the independence of the electoral committee, adding that the committee conducted the exercise without interference. “To the best of my knowledge, it is free and fair. The electoral committee is independent,” he said. On the security arrangements, Odogwu explained that approval had been obtained from the Inspector-General of Police for the conduct of the election. “We are all law-abiding citizens, but when it comes to election time, security must be present because anything can happen,” he said. He said the association adopted a cluster-by-cluster voting system, under which votes were counted in each cluster before being forwarded to the collation centre. On his re-election, Odogwu said his administration would build on the achievements of its first tenure and intensify efforts to address the challenges facing traders and businesses in the complex. “In our first tenure, by the grace of God, we delivered a lot of projects. Now that we have been voted back, we are going to do more,” he said. The Chairman of the Lagos Cluster, Chief Christopher Lucas, and a voter, Mrs Patricia Umenze, also described the election as peaceful. item.title: Nvidia board puts Jensen Huang back as boss
item.description: There's no telling what caused the Nvidia board to unanimously vote to reinstate Huang less than a week after saying his return wasn’t under consideration - except reportedly the threat of having one's head ripped off and brain peed on - but that really doesn't matter, at least as far as shareholders need to be concerned: Jensen's back in charge and all’s right in the world of chip stocks. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said of the decision to reinstate him, calling it an honor. Nvidia kicked its former-cum-current CEO and president to the curb on November 12, but not over allegations that he may have been sleeping with a suspected Chinese spy - it was affairs at Nvidia with his subordinates that appears to have been the last straw with Nvidia directors. Nvidia stock has tumbled since Huang’s ouster, and much of the rest of the tech stock world followed suit . Nvidia insiders and tech heavyweights have been pushing for Huang’s return for about as long as he was unemployed, but calls for his return from the US federal government may have been the catalyst for a change of heart among Nvidia leadership who didn’t want Huang back. "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk," Nvidia said in its statement announcing Huang’s return. "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," board chair Harvey Jones added. Jones was made Nvidia's first board chair upon Huang’s resignation, and will remain in that role. It's not clear what senior levels of the US government weighed in on Huang's return, but President Donald Trump opined that the company had made "the correct and proper decision" in welcoming Huang back. "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security," Trump said in a post on Truth Social. "The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." ®

item.title: Bitcoin Price Surges Above $64,000 as Nvidia Reinstates CEO
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Surges Above $64,000 as Nvidia Reinstates CEO The bitcoin price surged to above $64,000 on Monday morning, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive and sent stocks sharply higher. Bitcoin is up about $8,500 from its weekend low of roughly $55,100, which came at about 1:17 a.m. ET on Saturday. Nvidia’s board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, the company said Monday morning. The board said it spoke with Huang and received input from “senior levels of the United States government,” concluding that his return “poses no national security risk.” Nvidia board restores Huang after 12 days Huang resigned on Nov. 11 after reports of an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials believe is a Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress took over as interim CEO. The board has said an investigation into the reported foreign intelligence effort will continue, and Huang said he supports it. Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said the board believes Huang “is the right person to lead” the company. Huang called it an honor to return and said he “can’t wait to get back to work.” The company also formed a national security and export control committee and is searching for a chief compliance officer. The stock had lost nearly half its value during a seven-week losing streak, even after Nvidia reported better-than-expected quarterly results on Nov. 17. Investors worried about life without Huang, and bitcoin traded in step with the rout in technology shares. Nvidia (NVDA) shares were up roughly 31% to near $165 in premarket trading. Shares had tumbled 14% on Friday, closing out that seventh straight weekly decline, after a report that the SEC is examining the company’s accounting. Nasdaq-100 futures were up about 6.6% and S&P 500 futures about 4.2% at 9:21 a.m. ET. Crypto stocks and miners jump Bitcoin-linked equities rallied with the chipmaker. Coinbase (COIN) was up about 9% to near $111 in premarket trading, and Strategy (MSTR) gained about 16% to near $90.50. Miners with AI data center businesses led the move, with IREN up about 27%, MARA up about 16%, Riot Platforms (RIOT) up about 14% and Core Scientific (CORZ) up about 17%. Strategy also disclosed in an 8-K that it bought 457 bitcoin last week at an average of about $64,898, lifting its total to 851,305 BTC. The company’s average cost is about $75,446 per coin, so its stack is still under water at current prices. Weekend low and a bruised market The rally follows a brutal stretch. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.28% on Friday, and the S&P 500 lost 8.61% for the week while the Nasdaq dropped 10.02%. Bitcoin slid with stocks and finished last week down about 6%, its seventh straight red weekly candle. Spot bitcoin ETFs shed about $1.79 billion last week, their fourth straight week of net outflows, including roughly $669 million on Friday. He added: “the Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” He called Huang “a Great Patriot.” Trump said Nvidia should press on with an internal investigation into its compliance with US rules designed to keep China from obtaining the company’s most advanced chips for training and running AI models. item.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior US government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead,” the company said in a statement. Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board. The decision came three days after Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.” Trump described Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions,” and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart.” Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused. Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.” Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips. US intelligence services reportedly concluded she passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations. Board chair Harvey Jones said Monday that directors now believe Huang “is the right person to lead Nvidia” and that his return serves the interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers. Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive who was named Nvidia’s first-ever board chair during the crisis, will stay in the role. Chief financial officer Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, will continue as CFO. Nvidia said a committee of independent directors set up earlier this month to investigate whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort will see its probe through to the end. Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating, the company said. Vanguard News The post Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues The U.K. will bar crypto exchange operators from trading against their own capital on the venues they run, while a new Treasury order clears independent market makers to trade on those platforms without a separate dealing permission. The Financial Conduct Authority’s final rules say a firm “must not execute any orders against its proprietary capital” on a qualifying trading platform it operates. The FCA’s guidance spells out the effect: a firm “cannot act as a market maker” on its own platform. The restriction takes effect Oct. 25, 2027. The FCA rule itself is not new. The regulator published it on June 30 in policy statement PS26/11, part of a five-document package that completed its crypto rulebook. What changed last week was the Treasury’s side of the framework. What the FCA rule covers The FCA’s rulebook defines a market maker as a person who holds themselves out on a platform on a continuous basis as willing to buy and sell qualifying cryptoassets against their own capital at prices they set. That is the activity operators will be barred from on their own venues. There is one carve-out. An operator with the appropriate permission may still engage in matched principal trading to execute client orders on its platform, as long as it follows the platform’s non-discretionary rules. The FCA warned that this model does not rule out settlement risk, so firms should take steps to minimize it. The bar applies only to the operator’s own platform. Under the same rules, an operator with the right permission can still trade against its own capital outside the venue it runs. It must make clear to clients which capacity it is acting in, and it must manage conflicts of interest. Treasury clears outside market makers The Treasury made the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2026 on Nov. 18. They add a new Article 9UA to the U.K.’s crypto legislation. The article carves two kinds of activity out of the regulated activity of dealing in qualifying cryptoassets as principal. One is activity carried on “otherwise than for the purpose of providing a service to another person.” The other is activity carried on “as a market maker on a qualifying cryptoasset trading platform.” In practice, a third-party firm quoting prices on a U.K. crypto platform would not need the principal-dealing permission for that activity. The text does not say who the market maker has to be, so the bar on operators comes from the FCA’s rules rather than from the Treasury order. The explanatory note says no impact assessment was prepared because no significant new costs are expected. The FCA’s rules also put new duties on platforms that rely on market makers. Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating, the company said. Shares of Nvidia rocketed about 30 percent higher in pre-market trading Monday as the tech giant announced it reinstated Huang. item.title: Eurozone business activity still growing despite French downturn
item.description: Business activity in the euro area registered a “steady” expansion this month, a key survey showed Monday, as faster growth in Germany helped counter a deepening downturn in France. The eurozone purchasing managers’ index (PMI) published by S&P Global, a gauge of the economy’s overall health, stood at 51.7 in November, unchanged from October, but below the 52.0 forecast of economists surveyed by FactSet. A reading above 50 indicates growth while one below 50 signals contraction. “At the headline level, the flash PMI data signal sustained steady growth for the eurozone in November, consistent with the economy growing at a near 0.3 percent pace in the fourth quarter,” S&P chief business economist Chris Williamson said in a statement. But he cautioned that the “overall picture of continuing economic resilience masks worrying divergences in performance within the euro area.” “While growth in Germany has accelerated to the fastest for four and a half years, as its manufacturing sector enjoys a growth spurt of the likes not seen for over five years, France is suffering a deepening downturn,” Williamson said. The German economy, he said, was benefiting strongly from “surging investment spending on defence and AI-related technologies”. At the same time, “uncertainty about the political environment, social unrest and the high cost of living are hitting service providers especially hard, especially for consumer-facing businesses, dampening growth both in France and across the rest of the region as a whole”. The European Central Bank has lifted borrowing costs twice this year in response to the energy shock triggered by the US war on Iran, and Williamson warned that “higher interest rates are also starting to show up as an increasing drag”. He noted that lower oil prices had “helped tame inflationary pressures” somewhat in November. But he predicted the PMI data alongside a “broad message” of eurozone growth would bolster calls for a further rate increase in December. The post Eurozone business activity still growing despite French downturn appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Murray-Bruce hails Tinubu’s CNG bus initiative, urges governors to act
item.description: Former Senator Ben Murray-Bruce has commended President Bola Tinubu’s initiative to introduce compressed natural gas (CNG)-powered buses and promote local vehicle assembly, urging state governors to invest in the programme and supporting infrastructure. Murray-Bruce, founder of Silverbird Group, made the call in a Facebook post on Monday, describing the initiative as a step towards transforming Nigeria from a consumer nation into a producer economy. He welcomed the Federal Government’s partnership with Chinese automobile manufacturer Yutong to supply 100 CNG buses to Lagos State by December, followed by plans for local assembly in Ibadan, Oyo State. According to the former lawmaker, local assembly of the buses would create employment and ensure that more economic benefits remain within the country. “Every bus we assemble at home is a salary paid at home,” he said. Murray-Bruce also highlighted the impact of CNG-powered public transportation on commuters, citing a reduction in transport fares on the Enugu-Nsukka route from N4,000 to N1,600. He said the reduction would provide relief for students, traders, healthcare workers and other commuters struggling with transportation costs. “The numbers already speak. On the Enugu to Nsukka route, the fare has fallen from N4,000 to N1,600. For a student, a trader, or a nurse, that is not a statistic. That is dinner,” he said. The former senator urged state governors to take advantage of the Federal Government’s initiative by procuring CNG buses, investing in refuelling infrastructure and addressing long queues at existing CNG stations. “Now, my dear governors, the President has opened the door. Walk through it. Buy the buses, build the refuelling stations, and end the long CNG queues before they become the new fuel queues,” he said. He argued that the success of the country’s economic reforms should be measured by their impact on the daily lives of Nigerians, particularly through reduced transportation costs. “Reform is not a speech. Reform is a cheaper ride to work,” Murray-Bruce added. The post Murray-Bruce hails Tinubu’s CNG bus initiative, urges governors to act appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: France Detains Three Over Mystery Train Accident
item.description: French police on Monday arrested three people at a traveller camp in connection with the September derailment of a train that injured 44 people, two sources with knowledge of the matter said. In France, the term “travellers” refers to communities who maintain an itinerant lifestyle, including some of Romani origin. The train, carrying 186 passengers, derailed on September 11 between the cities of Rouen and Caen in Normandy, northwestern France. Railway workers work on the removal of a derailed train carriage in Cleon, northwestern France, on September 16, 2026. Photo by GUILLAUME SALIGOT / AFP Prosecutors at the time said the driver had tested negative for alcohol or drugs and that a section of rail found on the track may have caused the derailment. A local official said the fragment weighed around 300 kilograms. Police on Monday detained a 45-year-old and his 22-year-old twin sons at the camp near the site of the accident, one of the sources told AFP. They were taken into police custody on suspicion of attempted theft, theft committed by a group, and involuntary bodily injury, the source said. After the derailment, President Emmanuel Macron warned of the growing threat posed by Moscow’s shadow operations across Europe, saying he had ordered measures to protect France’s critical infrastructure. item.description: Iranian courts have demanded that the United States pay $290 billion in damages, a judiciary official said on Monday. “We have secured court rulings in domestic courts awarding $290 billion in damages against the Americans,” said Hassan Abdolianpour, head of the judiciary’s centre for lawyers, according to state television. He also said that several lawsuits have been filed against the Gulf Arab nations for “allowing their territory to be used by America to launch attacks against Iran”. According to state TV, the damages cover US actions going back decades. File photo showing US-Iran flags. The Middle East war began on February 28 when the United States and Israel launched a wave of strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, saying it is targeting US-Israeli bases and assets in those countries. The Islamabad memorandum of understanding signed in June between the US and Iran, which aimed to pave the way to a peace deal, included a clause that would see Washington and its regional partners drawing up a plan with at least $300 billion “for the reconstruction and economic development” of Iran. Moreover, Iran has been under crippling sanctions by the United States for decades, mainly over its nuclear program. That assurance comes despite Huang's admitted affair with a woman who, US intelligence sources believe, was working as a Chinese spy and allegations that Nvidia had subverted export controls meant to keep Nvidia chips from reaching China. It also comes despite multiple developing investigations from multiple different government departments into those and other alleged national security, accounting, and corporate governance failures. item.title: Scramble To Save Climate Fight After COP Collapse
item.description: Officials voiced dismay on Monday at the collapse of UN climate talks, urging the world not to abandon joint efforts to curb the deadly warming of the planet. A final agreement was rejected on Sunday at the COP31 climate summit, with delegates failing to strike an agreement over fossil fuels amid resistance from oil-producing countries. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres voiced “profound frustration” while key player China expressed disappointment — but insisted the green transition was “irreversible”. COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (C) attends a plenary session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Centre, in Antalya on November 22, 2026. The EU issued a plea to salvage multilateral efforts to fight climate change, which is worsening the risk and impact of deadly storms, floods and droughts. “It is absolutely crucial that the multilateral process stays alive,” said European Commission spokeswoman Anna-Kaisa Itkonen, calling the talks’ failure a “terrible outcome”. Familiar fault lines emerged at COP31 over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. Oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal at the conference co-hosted by Turkey and Australia. Negotiations chair Chris Bowen who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. Geopolitical worries Australian Minister for Climate Change and Energy and President of COP31 Negotiations Chris Bowen (C) and COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (3rd R) and delegates before a session during the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center, in Antalya, on November 22, 2026. Photo by YASIN AKGUL / AFP Bowen, Australia’s climate minister, said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from heatwaves in Europe to floods in Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. Faced with oil producers’ resistance, Ireland’s climate minister Darragh O’Brien vowed: “We will not endorse a cover decision … that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change.” O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, added: “We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.” Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record, running two days past schedule. item.title: Everything going down at once wasn't evidence of a conspiracy – but the truth may be scarier
item.description: Have you or someone you love been affected by a tech outage this week? Yeah, us too. You can listen to the latest episode of The Kettle right here on this page, as well as on Spotify , Apple Music , or YouTube . Those platforms also let you subscribe to The Kettle, so you are always notified when the latest episode goes live In a week of big stories the biggest one seems to be the fact that everyone from Microsoft to the NSA was dealing with outages , and here's what might be the worst part: It doesn't seem to be AI, nor hostile countries intent on destroying our infrastructure. Unfortunately for all of us, what the past week of outages reveal is that – as we discussed on The Kettle less than a month ago – all of our essential tech infrastructure is basically held together with duct tape and twine. Join host Brandon Vigliarolo , cybersecurity editor Jessica Lyons , and open source reporter Liam Proven to discuss what comes next, and whether we can fix any of this without tearing all of it out and starting from scratch. A lightly edited transcript is included below: Brandon (00:04) Hi everyone and welcome to the latest episode of the Register's Kettle podcast. I'm your host, Reg reporter Brandon Vigliarolo, and if you're hearing this, then that means there isn't an outage right now, which seems like that might be a lot to ask of our technology in the past week. It's been a busy week. We had Anthropic's IPO , Nvidia drama continuing , and other stuff going on. But the one thing that everyone seems to be talking about is what's become known in the zeitgeist as Outagepalooza, as it seems like everything was offline at some point in the past few days. With me to discuss the chaos and the conspiracy theories they're giving rise to is Reg cybersecurity editor Jessica Lyons and our open source reporter Liam Proven. Guys, what's happening? Jessica Lyons (00:45) I've got my tinfoil hat on right now, so I'm ready. Brandon (00:48) Yes, I've had family calling me being like, my god, what's happening? Who's ending the world right now? Is it AI? Jessica Lyons (00:55) Ha ha ha. Brandon (00:56) We'll get to that part. Liam Proven (00:57) Wonderful. My mum's wardrobe door stuck this week and we found a company on the little rock in the middle of the Irish Sea that fixes sliding doors and he didn't get my emails because he's one hundred percent Microsoft and he uses Hotmail and it's Hotmail. Liam Proven (01:18) And when I got it through, you'd be amazed at the ramifications. I SMS'd him in the end and he got that and then was really angry because I said, "Dude, I've been trying to get you for three days. Can you at least reply and say Friday?" And he's like, "No, I've got no email, I've got no internet, I've got nothing." Brandon (01:32) My god. Yes, it's been an interesting week. So Jess, catch us up on everything that's fallen apart in the past few days. We've got quite a list growing here. Jessica Lyons (01:40) Yes. Well, we'll start with Outlook. I'm sorry, Mic

item.title: Woman arrested for assaulting policeman in Abia
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Abia State Police Command has arrested a woman, identified as Ettoh Barkerk, for allegedly assaulting a police inspector and tearing his uniform during an operation in Aba. The suspect was arrested after police officers from the Ndiegoro Division responded to a distress call reporting that hoodlums were attacking members of the congregation at Christ the King Catholic Church (CKC), Aba. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Maureen Chinaka, who confirmed the incident, said the suspect allegedly became violent when officers arrived at the scene, assaulted one of them and attempted to retrieve recovered exhibits. According to Chinaka, the incident occurred on November 22, 2026, when the division received information that some hoodlums were throwing fireworks indiscriminately within the church premises, causing panic and threatening public peace. She said a patrol team was immediately deployed to the area to contain the situation, prevent further escalation and restore order. “Upon receipt of the report, a patrol team from the Division swiftly mobilised to the scene to contain the situation, prevent further escalation and restore public order. In the course of the operation, one Ettoh Barkerk (female) was apprehended at the scene with fireworks in her possession. “However, the suspect became violent and physically assaulted an Inspector attached to the patrol team, tore his uniform and attempted to forcibly retrieve the recovered exhibits. “The suspect was subsequently subdued and arrested, while the recovered fireworks and other relevant exhibits were secured for investigation. She will be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigation,” she said. The police spokesperson said the command condemned the alleged assault, describing it as unacceptable conduct that fell short of the standards of civility and respect for the law. She added that normalcy had been restored within the church premises, while security monitoring had been intensified in the area to prevent further breaches of public peace. item.title: Strategy (MSTR) Adds 457 Bitcoin for $29.6 million
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategy (MSTR) Adds 457 Bitcoin for $29.6 million Strategy (MSTR) bought 457 bitcoin last week for $29.6 million at an average of about $64,898 per coin, an 8-K filing shows, lifting its total to 851,305 BTC as the bitcoin price trades about under the company’s average cost. The purchase ran from Nov. 16 to Nov. 22. Strategy said it paid $64.23 billion for its stack, an average of $75,446 per coin including fees and expenses. That is $6 below the $75,452 average it reported a week earlier, so the new coins barely moved the cost basis. The buy is also smaller than the 485 bitcoin Strategy added the week before . Strategy shares were trading near $83.50 in premarket on Monday, up about 7% from Friday’s close near $78. How Strategy paid for the coins Strategy funded the purchase entirely with common stock. It sold 1,925,676 MSTR shares under its at-the-market program for net proceeds of $176.7 million, and no preferred stock was sold during the week. Only $29.6 million of that cash went into bitcoin. The rest went to buy back Strategy’s own STRC preferred stock, which is the pattern the company has followed for several weeks. Strategy repurchased 2,183,747 STRC shares for $211.8 million. It paid $147.0 million of that with MSTR proceeds and $64.8 million from its USD Cash balance. The preferred buyback was roughly seven times the bitcoin spend. The board also lifted the size of its digital credit securities repurchase program from $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion. After the increase, $1.12 billion remains available. About $17.9 billion of MSTR stock is still available under the ATM. The 457 coins were bought at an average of $64,898, which is above where bitcoin trades now. They also continue a slowdown: Strategy added 1,036 bitcoin in its Nov. 9 filing, 485 in its Nov. 16 filing and 457 in the latest one, while the preferred buybacks have grown. The stack equals about 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. Last week’s $29.6 million bitcoin spend was about 17% of the $176.7 million the ATM raised. Weekend low put Strategy deep under water Bitcoin hit a weekend low near $55,100, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. At that level, Strategy’s coins were worth about 27% less than the $75,446 it paid on average. The price has since recovered to around $61,000. At that level the 851,305 bitcoin are worth roughly $52 billion, about $12 billion below what Strategy paid. That is a paper loss only, since the filing shows no bitcoin sales during the week and the coins are still on the balance sheet. The slide has hit the stock hard. Strategy shares tumbled for a sixth straight day to about $86 on Thursday, and they fell again on Friday. A week ago the company said it was holding bitcoin modestly below cost , and the gap has widened since. Cash reserve moves to general use Strategy also changed how it labels its dollar cash. item.title: England launches world’s largest AI-aided breast cancer screening trial
item.description: England’s state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world’s largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years. The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset. The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians’ time. The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS. “This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world,” Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech’s “huge potential” while pledging “proper safeguards” to ensure safety and effectiveness. “If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery.” The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England. Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out. The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel. The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two. Recruitment has started at Cambridge University Hospitals, in eastern England, with more of the 30 selected sites opening in the coming months. Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women, with around 55,000 diagnosed every year in the UK. Women aged 50 to 71 are invited for screening every three years, amounting to around 2.1 million screenings annually. The NHS estimates this helps prevent around 1,300 deaths. A study published in The Lancet medical journal in January said that AI can improve breast cancer detection through more effective screening while reducing radiologists’ workloads. It analysed nearly 106,000 mammograms performed in Sweden as part of its national breast cancer screening programme — involving women with a median age of 53 — from April 2021 to early December 2022. item.title: Shettima tasks stakeholders on implementation of drug control plan
item.description: ….AGF, Marwa say new NDCMP will strengthen NDLEA; ECOWAS, Reps commend initiative By Kingsley Omonobi Vice-President Kashim Shettima has urged federal and state governments, the National Assembly, private sector operators and other stakeholders to ensure the effective implementation of the National Drug Control Master Plan (NDCMP) 2026–2030. Shettima said the five-year plan must be implemented with urgency, discipline and accountability, stressing that drug control should remain a national priority. The Vice-President spoke on Monday in Abuja as Special Guest of Honour at the official launch of the plan, which he commended to all institutions and stakeholders on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. Represented by the Special Adviser to the President on Special Duties, Office of the Vice-President, Dr Modibbo Aliyu Umar, Shettima said Nigeria could not secure its future without protecting the people responsible for building it. He described drug abuse and trafficking as public health concerns, security threats, development challenges and economic issues, warning that enforcement alone would not address the problem without prevention, treatment and measures to tackle illicit financial flows sustaining drug markets. “Our response must therefore be comprehensive, coordinated and sustained,” he said. Shettima identified the six pillars of the new plan as Supply Reduction; Drug Demand Reduction; Access to Controlled Medicines for Scientific and Medical Purposes; Alternative Development and Sustainable Livelihoods; Disruption of the Illicit Drug Economy; and Governance, Financing and Coordination. He commended the leadership of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), under Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), for making Nigeria the first African country to commence an Alternative Development programme, whose pilot project is being implemented in three communities in Ondo State. He urged state and local governments to embrace the initiative and take ownership of its implementation. On funding, the Vice-President warned that a national policy without a credible financing framework risked becoming a mere declaration of good intentions. He, therefore, directed that the plan’s priorities be incorporated into institutional work plans, budget proposals and implementation schedules. He challenged stakeholders to identify immediate actions their respective institutions must take to ensure the success of the initiative, insisting that global challenges should not become an excuse for inaction. “Five years from now, the significance of today’s launch will not be judged by the ceremony,” he said. “Let this be the moment Nigeria moves from policy to action.” In his welcome address, NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Marwa, said the new master plan was designed to consolidate previous achievements, address identified shortcomings and respond to emerging drug-related threats. item.title: COP31 collapse has shattered the pretence of a global climate consensus
item.description: A closing plenary session at the COP31 climate summit on 22 November AP Photo/Khalil Hamra/Alamy A deep rift among nations on how to tackle climate change, and whether the global economy can be weaned off fossil fuels, was exposed after the spectacular collapse of talks at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. After a tortuous fortnight of negotiations, COP31 ended in disarray late on 22 November after countries including the UK and the EU refused to agree to a political accord that failed to mention fossil fuels. Read more Can everyone live a ‘good life’ without destroying the planet? The Antalya pact would have seen countries officially recognise that the world is on course to exceed 1.5°C degrees of warming and promise to limit the scale of the overshoot as far as possible. It also would have committed nations to increasing the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 per cent globally by 2035, a key target for climate campaigners who see electrification as the route away from fossil-fuel dependency. Advertisement But the draft agreement proved unacceptable to many countries, including the UK, the EU and some small island nations, after all mentions of fossil fuels were omitted at the behest of fossil fuel-dependent nations such as Saudi Arabia and Russia. Failing to mention fossil fuels explicitly in the text would have marked a backwards step for the climate process, the EU argued. At COP28 in Dubai three years ago, nations agreed to “transition away from fossil fuels” , but since then, attempts to strengthen the language or clarify how this transition will take place have been blocked by petrostates. Alden Meyer at the climate think tank E3G says the talks were subjected to a “brutish” strategy from fossil fuel-exporting states to “systematically block” any reference to the COP28 deal. “They clearly have buyer’s remorse about that agreement. They never were happy about it.” Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter The EU also took issue with a paragraph inserted at the behest of Saudi Arabia – which leads the 22-member Arab group of countries – calling for the rapid growth of carbon capture and storage technologies to the gigatonne scale by 2035. Carbon capture and storage technologies are expensive and unproven at scale, and many sceptics are concerned that focusing on them will justify the continued use of fossil fuels and distract from the deep emissions cuts necessary for controlling climate change. Ireland’s climate minister Darragh O’ Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU, claimed the negotiations had been “hijacked by fossil fuel producers” and said the EU would “not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels”. Parties also vented their frustration at the hosts, Turkey and Australia, with the joint presidency leading to a sluggish and disjointed negotiating process in the final days of the summit. There was also disquiet from lower-income nations over the lack of new climate finance

item.title: Military air strikes kill 37 terrorists, destroy four vehicles
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian military says it has neutralised 37 terrorists and destroyed four vehicles in a series of precision air strikes conducted across the North-East between November 16 and 23, 2026. The operations, carried out by the Air Component of Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), also led to the destruction of a terrorist staging facility and disrupted suspected improvised explosive device (IED) activities along troops’ operational routes. Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force (North-East), Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, disclosed this on Monday, saying the air component conducted six precision strikes across five locations within the theatre during the period. He said the operations, supported by credible intelligence and persistent Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR), targeted terrorist movements, hideouts and logistics assets in Monguno Local Government Area, Kerenoa and Fage in Marte LGA, and the Tumbuma Baba general area of Kukawa LGA, Borno State. According to him, a pre-emptive air strike was conducted following intelligence gathering, with subsequent Battle Damage Assessment (BDA) confirming that 10 terrorists were neutralised, while several others sustained injuries. Goni said that in a separate operation on November 17, ISR surveillance identified a terrorist staging facility at Arina Chiki, where insurgents were reportedly planning an attack on troops’ defensive positions. He said the location was engaged with precision fire, with subsequent assessment confirming the destruction of the targeted building and no further movement observed within the structure. Similarly, on November 20, military surveillance assets identified two terrorist vehicles concealed near a tree in Kerenoa. The vehicles were engaged and destroyed in a precision air strike. On the same day, another terrorist vehicle was identified at a suspected IED assembly location in the Fage general area, where insurgents were reportedly preparing to plant explosives along a route used by troops. The vehicle was immediately engaged and destroyed, disrupting the suspected IED-related activity. Goni said further successes were recorded on November 23 in the Tumbuma Baba general area of Kukawa LGA, where an intelligence-led operation identified and destroyed another terrorist vehicle. During the operation, two suspected terrorists were observed emerging from a nearby life-support structure. He said persistent ISR subsequently tracked the suspects to a gathering of six other terrorists taking cover under a tree. After additional terrorists joined the group, a precision air strike was launched against the identified position. The subsequent BDA confirmed that all eight terrorists were neutralised, with no further movement observed at the location. item.title: F1 in Las Vegas: You've never seen an F1 race like this before
item.description: Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend. And for the first time since the event’s inception in 2023 , the Grand Prix delivered on a long-promised spectacle. The racing was closer to an IndyCar oval race than anything F1 fans will have seen since slipstreaming was the order of the day at places like Monza and Hockenheim, back when humans were still landing on the Moon and downforce had yet to fundamentally change racing. The Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar. It has plenty of long straights, so this year’s cars still suffer from energy starvation throughout the lap, as the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly , leaving the cars on just over half power with their V6 engines operating without the benefit of the hybrid’s electric motor. But the 17 turns are mostly all low speed, so there’s no risk of seeing the cars driving demoralizingly slowly through corners that are supposed to test one’s mettle . Read full article Comments

item.title: American Bitcoin (ABTC) Lands $150 Million Bitcoin-Backed Credit Line From FalconX
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine American Bitcoin (ABTC) Lands $150 Million Bitcoin-Backed Credit Line From FalconX American Bitcoin Corp. (ABTC) has secured a $150 million revolving credit facility from FalconX that is backed by its bitcoin, the miner said Monday, giving it a way to raise cash without selling coins from its reserve. The facility was signed by an American Bitcoin subsidiary and is secured by certain of the company’s bitcoin holdings. American Bitcoin said the money can go toward strategic growth opportunities and general corporate purposes. “This $150 million facility provides American Bitcoin with non-dilutive capital to support our continued operations and growth initiatives,” CEO Mike Ho said in the release. Terms of the FalconX facility The FalconX line is committed up to $150 million, and each draw is subject to bitcoin collateral requirements and other customary conditions. Because it is revolving, the company can draw, repay and redraw funds during the term. Borrowings carry a 5.95% loan fee, plus a commitment fee on any undrawn amount. The initial term is two years, with an optional three-year extension at FalconX’s discretion, subject to customary conditions. The company did not name the size of the commitment fee. The facility has an initial collateral ratio of 143%. At that level, drawing the full $150 million would require about $214.5 million in pledged bitcoin, or roughly 3,500 BTC with bitcoin trading near $61,300 early Monday. American Bitcoin did not say whether it has drawn on the line yet. Its release lists the risks, including the possible liquidation of pledged bitcoin if its value falls below required levels, and requirements to post more collateral or repay borrowings on short notice. “Collateralized lending gives American Bitcoin a way to access liquidity while it continues to grow its Bitcoin reserve and scale its business,” said Oliver Sitt, a sales director at FalconX. The prime broker said the deal shows how it can structure working capital for public companies that do not want to sell their holdings. FalconX provides financing, trading and asset management services to institutional clients. A miner that has avoided selling its reserve American Bitcoin is majority-owned by Hut 8 and counts Eric Trump as a co-founder and chief strategy officer. On its third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 4, the company said it held 8,427 BTC at the end of September and that its reserve had since passed 8,500 BTC. Eric Trump said on the call that the company did not buy any bitcoin on the open market in the quarter or issue shares through its at-the-market program. Every coin added came from its own mining, though the company did sell part of its production to cover operating costs. It mined about 891 BTC in the third quarter, down from 932 in the second. The company reported net income of $126 million, largely from gains on its bitcoin as the price rose about 39% in the quarter. That price has since reversed. Bitcoin ended September nea

item.title: Trump says he won't allow US companies to build datacenters abroad
item.description: US President Donald Trump has threatened a "tremendous tax" on American companies building datacenters overseas, arguing that the infrastructure should stay at home to preserve the country's AI lead over China. Speaking at a White House press conference after returning from the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Trump portrayed AI leadership as a contest America could not afford to lose. Trump went on to say that "we're not going to allow our companies to build datacenters outside of our country," adding that "they allowed that to happen with chips and everything else and it was very destructive to our country." The threat appeared to catch even his own administration unbriefed. "I haven't even said that to my people, but I'm telling them now," Trump said. The Official White House Rapid Response account posted a video clip on X. We asked the White House if the president intends to follow through, and we will let you know if we get an answer. Trump said: "We're not going to allow companies to build datacenters in other countries. If they do that, they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them. We want them to do it here." The threat comes amid concerns that Chinese entities were able to use Nvidia's cutting-edge GPUs for training AI models by accessing cloud services hosted in third countries. The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued new rules to try and crack down on this practice last week. "We're not allowing datacenters to go into other countries, as China will take all of them, and we're not allowing that to happen," Trump repeated. "We're going to put tremendous penalties on companies that try and do it. They want to build that one in Finland, and we're not allowing that to happen," he added. Google is expanding its facilities in Finland, including one recently in the news because the developer had reportedly illegally felled 250,000 trees to make way for it. Such a policy seems unlikely to be allowed by Congress, where both houses will be under the control of the Democrats when the new term begins in January. Amazon, Google, and Microsoft already operate global datacenter networks to serve customers in different regions. Restrictions on further overseas construction would complicate those businesses. Omdia chief analyst Roy Illsley expressed doubt that this is a serious threat. "There will be ways around that if he does impose some executive order, and the ability to build datacenters is not just an American skill, many countries can build them, it is the equipment in them that is mostly US," he told The Register . "So I do not take this seriously as it would not work, there is no such thing as a US datacenter, they are made up of thousands of components from all over the globe. He could stop US capital from being invested in those countries, but that could have trade consequences." Mike Kharchenko of European hosting firm HostZealot said there are good reasons why the c

item.title: I’m planning my first dark sky trip, and all because this educational star projector showed me what I’m missing
item.description: I didn’t expect much as I unboxed the Brainstorm Night Sky; after all, I’m significantly older than this educational star projector’s target audience. Perhaps I’d come away with a sense of wonder and delight, coupled with mild irritation at having to hunt down three AA batteries to power it. Instead, I was filled with envy as the Brainstorm Night Sky reminded me just what I was missing, thanks to the rigors of light pollution . A few minutes after powering it down, I was already making plans for my first dark sky trip, yearning for a view that rivaled the Brainstorm’s cosmic images. Brainstorm Night Sky Projector review Whatever your age, the Brainstorm Night Sky is so simple to use The Brainstorm Night Sky projector comes with four or six slides, depending on whether you buy the blue or gray version (Image credit: Chris McMullen) Draw the curtains, press the Night Sky’s single button (tilting the projector and twisting the focus as appropriate) and it projects a circular image onto a ceiling or wall. Press the button again and the projection slowly begins to rotate, slowly but stutter-free. It really is that simple to operate and, aimed at budding astronomers aged eight or above, it's reasonably lightweight without feeling flimsy. Depending on the model you buy, you’ll get four or six interchangeable slides. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) Specifications Weight: 14.8 oz (420 g) Bulb type: Non-specified Laser: No Control: On-unit Rotation: Yes, one speed Projection area: Up to 8.2 ft (2.5 m) Sleep timer: Yes (30 mins) Power: 3x AA batteries Speaker: No I was initially a little surprised by the size of the projection: at up to 8.2 feet (2.5 m) wide it’s not going to fill an entire ceiling. It also switches off after 30 minutes, a limit that can’t be disabled, so if you’re looking to put on your own space-themed party this is not the projector for you. But it’s on point for home education and, priced from $49.99, the Brainstorm Night Sky projector won’t break the bank. There’s minimal distortion around the edge of the images; the planets are spherical from the word go, unlike some projectors where I’ve had to tweak them to stop Mars turning into an egg. And I never once had to crane my neck because half the solar system had been projected onto a bookcase. item.title: What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?
item.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been. So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure? Last of the Soviet space explorers Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June. A model of one of the Phobos spacecraft on display in the Memorial Museum of Cosmonautics in Moscow, Russia. (Image credit: Музей Космонавтики from Россия, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons) To say that a lot hinged on the success of the mission would be an understatement, given the unfortunate fate of the probe's predecessor, Phobos 1, which went offline on Sept. 2, 1988, after a faulty command sequence was initiated while the spacecraft was on its way to Mars. The stakes were almost immediately raised as Phobos 2 arrived in orbit around Mars on Jan. 30, 1989 , when one of the probe's three onboard flight system processors was found to have gone offline, with another already experiencing technical issues. Over the course of the next several weeks, Phobos 2 was able to overcome some of these setbacks and successfully began sending useful scientific data about the Martian environment back to Earth. By March, all the probe's science instruments appeared to be functioning normally, and despite the earlier loss of one of its processors, the remaining two had continued to facilitate control of the spacecraft by its Soviet ground control team. An image of Phobos captured by the Soviet Union's Phobos 2 probe. (Image credit: Roscosmos) Unexplained failure That all changed on March 27, 1989, as Phobos 2 prepared to capture navigational ima
